Perturbation, Not Provenance: Why Activation Steering Does Not Make a Robust Text Watermark
扰动，而非来源：为何激活引导不能构成稳健的文本水印
Sergey Pletenev
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Linear directions in the activation space of large language models causally and universally influence model behavior. This suggests that they might serve as a basis for a robust text watermark. The idea is to steer the generation along a specific semantic direction and then recover the mark by probing the activations of the re-encoded text. We test this hypothesis by conducting a series of experiments. We vary the strength of the steering and use four different directions (formality, sentiment, complexity, and a random control) across two different model families. We also test two paraphrasing attacks: a sentence-level one and a stronger paragraph-level one. The results show that activation-steering watermarks are outperformed by a standard logit-based watermark (KGW) in terms of detection accuracy. At a matched level of fluency (within 1.15 times the original text's perplexity), KGW achieved an AUC of 0.81 against a sentence-level paraphraser, while the best steering direction only reached 0.65. A stronger paragraph-level paraphraser lowered both (0.65 for KGW and 0.59 for steering), narrowing the gap but not reversing it. On Qwen, it left the two indistinguishable but at near-chance levels for both. We further showed that the detectability provided by steering was not semantic: a random direction was just as detectable as a meaningful one. The signal was independent of which layer was probed and whether a surface feature control was used. We conclude that, in this case, semantic activation does not encode a localized, recoverable semantic mark, but rather a global, content-independent shift that can only be strongly detected when the text is degraded.

diffusion

Abstract
Diffusion language models apply bidirectional attention over the whole context at every denoising step, so a longer context makes each step substantially more expensive. Sparsifying only at inference leaves the pretrained weights unchanged, so the model is never trained under the sparse pattern it runs with. We propose Prefilling-dLLM v2, which continues training a diffusion language model so that it routes with its native mask token. One mask is appended at the end of each chunk, and a learned role offset marks it as a routing slot. On every fourth layer, a query keeps a bidirectional local window and the top-K chunks scored from that mask; the other layers use a bidirectional sliding window. Starting from Dream-v0-Base-7B extended to 16K with YaRN, we compare Prefilling-dLLM v2 with bidirectional NSA, DSA, and SWA under the same layout, key budget, and dense initialization, using the same Fast-dLLM decoder. With the YaRN factor scaled to the evaluation length, Prefilling-dLLM v2 leads the other sparse methods on all three RULER tasks from 16K to 128K. Its mean accuracy at 128K is 7.4 points above NSA, the next sparse model, while DSA and SWA remain near zero. At the same length, decoding is 172x faster than with full dense attention.

Batch-Paced: Fixed-Budget Batch Decoding in Discrete Diffusion Language Models

Shuai Zhang, Zhanchao Zhou, Huachuan Qiu, Anqi Li, Zhenzhong Lan
cs.CL
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
As generative language models become more capable and widely used, inference demand grows, making efficient serving increasingly important. Discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs) offer a promising path to more efficient inference through parallel token generation. Prior dLLM decoding methods, however, focus on improving inference efficiency for individual sequences. We formulate fixed-budget dLLM batch decoding and introduce Batch-Paced, a training-free method that jointly optimizes the allocation of decoding compute across requests to improve overall batch quality. Across two dLLM backbones, five benchmarks and their representative mixtures, Batch-Paced improves batch performance under matched budgets; gains generally grow with batch size and largely persist across decoding configurations. Analysis of requests' decoding trajectories suggests that these gains arise largely by raising the committed-token confidence of lower-confidence requests. We further show that Batch-Paced's batch decode time remains competitive and that adding a decoding-depth allowance during Batch-Paced decoding can shorten it further at a modest performance cost.

Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
Agent-Reflex：教会语言智能体进行反思性行动
Guanting Dong, Xinyu Yang, Jiajie Jin, Yuyang Hu, Xiaoshuai Song, Yifei Chen, Xiaoxi Li, Jiejun Tan, Yutao Zhu, Tat-Seng Chua, Ji-Rong Wen, Zhicheng Dou
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models have evolved from single-turn chatbots into interactive agents capable of long-horizon reasoning. In real deployments, MCP tool services can return noisy feedback and users may intervene to correct the agent, but existing methods provide limited supervision for reflection learning and failure recovery. To bridge this gap, we propose Agent-Reflex, a general training framework for incentivizing proactive reflection in agents. Specifically, Agent-Reflex comprises three stages. First, Environment Reflection Skill Discovery (RSD) injects grounded tool-feedback perturbations into environment scaling, samples a capability-diverse LLM pool, mines matched success-failure pairs, and summarizes reusable reflection meta-skills. Building on this skill library, we then apply Reflective Supervised Fine-Tuning (ReSFT) that converts each skill into supervision for self-reflection, skill recovery, and user-centric correction, strengthening complementary reflective behaviors. Finally, we propose On-Policy Reflective Policy Optimization (ORPO) to combine agentic reinforcement learning under noisy interactions with reflection-guided on-policy distillation to further elicit proactive reflection. Built on Qwen3-8B, Agent-Reflex reaches 58.6 overall on five long-horizon tool-use benchmarks and 29.1 on AgentNoiseBench, surpassing strong environment-scaling and reflection baselines. Experiments on six challenging agent benchmark suites demonstrate the effectiveness of Agent-Reflex. Further analyses show that Agent-Reflex improves agents' robustness to noise while maintaining stable training dynamics, supporting scalable agent training. Our code is available at https://github.com/RUC-NLPIR/Agent-Reflex.

Virtual Head Attention
虚拟头注意力
Xibo Ding, Guoxia Wang, Jinle Zeng, Jiabin Yang, Sirui Tao, Chao Yang, Dianhai Yu
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
The design of attention mechanisms in long-context large language models faces an ``impossible triangle'' among KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality. GQA achieves strong quality but incurs high KV cache overhead; alternative approaches such as MLA and MFA can compress the cache, but MLA suffers from quality loss while MFA substantially increases training and prefill compute. We propose Virtual Head Attention (VHA), which simultaneously improves all three vertices through two lightweight linear operations: Q Premix applies a near-identity transformation to queries within each KV group to recover virtual head diversity from halved physical query heads, and Linear Postmix fuses inter-head features via a low-rank $I + AB^\top$ residual structure. Since VHA introduces no nonlinear operations, Premix can be folded into the query projection and Postmix into the output projection at inference time, reducing the model to a standard GQA-2 architecture that directly reuses all existing GQA inference optimizations. With only two KV heads, the group size in large models readily reaches 64, fully exploiting Tensor Core parallelism during decoding. Across four scales with 4K-context 50B-token pretraining, VHA consistently surpasses the standard GQA baseline at every scale ($+$0.05\% to $+$0.81\%), while reducing KV cache by $4\times$ vs.\ GQA-8 at dense scales and $2\times$ vs.\ GQA-4 at the MoE scale, and lowering training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9\% (1.7B, $S{=}4096$). On an industrial 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens at 8K context, VHA outperforms both MLA and GQA-4 by $+$0.70\,/\,$+$2.60\,\% on a 12-benchmark base-model evaluation suite; in a separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison after long-context mid-training, VHA attains an average RULER score of 84.4 over 8K--128K versus 73.0 for GQA, while using two rather than four KV heads in the full-attention layers.

Machine--human agreement in marking undergraduate assignments is specific to model, prompt and institution
在批改本科作业中，机器--人类一致性特定于模型、提示和机构
Giulio Corsi, Maryam Abo-Tabik, Yael Benn, Georgiana Thorpe Apreutesei, Roni Tibon, Alexandru Marcoci, Deborah Talmi
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) promise to automate one of higher education's most resource-intensive activities: assessing student writing. Existing evaluations are typically limited to a single model, a single prompt and a single institution. Using 761 undergraduate psychology assignments from three UK universities, we evaluated three frontier LLMs, individually and in ensemble, on accuracy, prompt sensitivity, error independence, generalisability and evidential basis. Agreement between human and machine marks varied widely, with no model or prompt optimal across institutions. All models compressed marks towards a common central tendency, overvaluing the weakest assignments and undervaluing the strongest. Because this error was shared, ensembling failed to remove it. Machine marks also rewarded linguistic features more strongly than human marks. Since human-machine agreement was a joint product of model, prompt and institution, we conclude that current LLMs lack evaluative capacity transferable across contexts, and that single-context validation overstates readiness for deployment.

SparPR: Runtime KV-Cache Recovery for Resource-Constrained LLM Inference on Consumer Hardware
SparPR：面向消费级硬件上资源受限 LLM 推理的运行时 KV 缓存恢复
Jieyun Deng, Keming Hu, Yanghe Liu, Li Feng
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Running large language models (LLMs) on consumer hardware is bottlenecked by the key-value (KV) cache, which grows with every decoded token and quickly exhausts the memory and bandwidth of a single consumer GPU. We present SparPR (Sparse Partial Recomputation), a runtime KV-cache recovery mechanism that does not modify model weights and requires no offline training. SparPR couples three online decisions: Query-Aware key-block selection scores historical blocks against the current query; dynamic budget control estimates per-block copy and recompute costs to decide how many blocks to retain; and on-demand local recomputation with cost-aware fallback merges retained blocks into continuous spans and switches between sparse recomputation and full recovery according to a runtime cost comparison. Implemented on FlexGen/FlexLLMGen, SparPR is evaluated on a single consumer laptop (RTX 3070 Ti 8GB, Ryzen 9 6900HX, 16GB RAM). It cuts end-to-end latency by 31%, 52%, and 63% at 1k, 2k, and 4k prompt tokens respectively, with 1.4x-2.7x higher throughput, and completes an 8k-token workload in 44 minutes where the FlexGen baseline times out. Under a fixed cache budget, SparPR retains a Needle Accuracy that stays well above StreamingLLM and H2O at every keep ratio, and ablation studies confirm that the three mechanisms act jointly.

Claim Framing as a Driver of LLM Sycophancy
主张表述框架作为大语言模型谄媚行为的驱动因素
Jean Seo, Pepa Atanasova, Isabelle Augenstein
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Sycophancy in Large Language Models, the tendency to align responses with user preferences over ground truth, has largely been studied using questions without a clear ground truth and with a single, plainly stated user opinion. We present a systematic study of which framings of a user's claim trigger sycophancy in factual question answering, where every answer is objectively verifiable without extra context. Evaluating 14 models on 42K questions, we express correct and incorrect user opinions through various claim framings over 8 dimensions and 21 types, and measure a broad set of opinion-driven behaviors. We find that all models are susceptible to user opinions regardless of size. Models are most influenced by how confidently an opinion is stated, whom it is attributed to, and whether it is presented as shared between the user and the model. In contrast to prior work, framings based on the user's expertise, authority over the model, or social pressure matter little in our factual setting. Larger models resist incorrect opinions better but are no better at recovering from their own errors. Our results call for sycophancy evaluations that probe how an opinion is framed, not merely whether one is present, and that measure multiple behaviors beyond a single flip rate.

TRACESTEER: Trace Driven Activation Steering for Hallucination Mitigation in Diffusion Language Models
TRACESTEER：轨迹驱动的激活引导用于扩散语言模型中的幻觉缓解

cs.CL
diffusionlarge language model
扩散模型相关
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive LLMs, yet remain susceptible to hallucination. Activation steering offers a promising mitigation approach by guiding parallel token predictions through internal representations. However, existing steering methods largely overlook two characteristics of dLLMs: dynamic denoising states and temporal hallucination risks, which challenge predefined steering vectors and uniform intervention strengths. We propose TRACESTEER, a trace-driven activation steering framework that uses preceding denoising predictions as feedback to jointly adapt steering direction and strength. Specifically, Denoising Feedback Steering (DF-Steering) constructs step-specific steering vectors from preceding predictions and current hidden states. Trajectory-Guided Steering Gate (TS-Gate) regulates their strength using prediction uncertainty and the denoising timestep. With the backbone frozen, factual supervision and magnitude regularization jointly guide the learning of adaptive steering interventions, promoting factual reliability and stability throughout denoising. Experiments on two dLLMs show improved factual reliability on TruthfulQA and generalization across five downstream benchmarks.

Are We Testing Too Much? A Survey of Benchmark Compression for Efficient Evaluation of Large Language Models
我们是否测试得太多了？面向大语言模型高效评测的基准压缩综述
Guoming Ling, Yupei Lin, Zhongzhan Huang, Junxin Li, Junjie Liu, Shanshan Zhong, Hefeng Wu, Liang Lin
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Benchmarks are essential for evaluating and improving large language models (LLMs). Yet many widely used benchmarks are redundant, making evaluation unnecessarily expensive. Benchmark compression lowers this cost by estimating full-benchmark scores and rankings from a partial evaluation. Research in this area has grown rapidly since 2024, but to our knowledge no survey has systematically organized its methods and findings. We review 119 papers to explain how methods choose what to evaluate, recover full-benchmark results, and verify their reliability. From this analysis, we develop a taxonomy covering compression within individual benchmarks, across benchmark suites, and during adaptive evaluation, together with work on redundancy and reliability. We compare their information needs, total costs, reliability checks, and limitations. Methods reduce evaluation costs by selecting representative subsets, using cheaper or reusable information, and testing adaptively, but risk poor coverage, inaccurate estimates, and sequential delays. The resulting taxonomy and practical guide help researchers choose, validate, and deploy methods for more efficient and reliable LLM evaluation.

Boya Zhang, Yuanchao Ma, Jiageng Wu, Krittaphas Chaisutyakorn, Rodrigo Gameiro, Ahram Han, Chien-Yu Huang, Nikhil Jaiswal, Marianna Leite, Miriam Mora-Mau, Jaime Pineda-Moreno, Siena Placino, Ryohei Yamamoto, Yugang Jia, Jie Yang, Leo Anthony Celi, Douglas Teodoro

Abstract
Pain is one of the most common and clinically important symptoms, reflecting disease onset, progression, and treatment response. However, pain is difficult to accurately capture and interpret from medical text, as its expression varies across languages, documentation types, and patient demographics, and is often embedded in terminology, negation, temporality, and contextual descriptions. Existing pain-related studies remain largely monolingual or limited to narrow clinical settings. In this study, we introduce PAINT, a multilingual framework for studying pain representation across medical exams and real-world clinical texts. PAINT includes nine pain-focused dataset partitions spanning English, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese, with clinician annotations in all four languages. We curated a structured schema covering pain relevance, pain presence, anatomical location, pain descriptors, and demographic information. To capture multilingual pain representations, we leverage large language models (LLMs) and adopt an ensemble strategy to improve performance. Ten clinicians across four languages validate the labels: the ensemble reaches macro-F1 of 0.91-1.00 on pain relevance and pain presence and 92-100% accuracy on demographics, with inter-annotator $κ$ of 0.82-1.00. We release the WorldMedQA-Pain ensemble labels, the extraction pipeline, validation scripts, and clinician annotation sheets for publicly licensed corpora, providing a foundation for pain-centered clinical NLP and for studying pain documentation across languages and healthcare contexts.

Lightweight but Linguistically Fair? Quantisation Robustness across Bavarian, German, and English

Jophin John, Michael Hoffmann, Piroska Lendvai, Florent Dufour
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Post-training quantisation reduces the memory cost of large language models, but it remains unclear whether compression preserves language skills of regional varieties as reliably as their standard-language counterparts. We study this question for Bavarian, Standard German, and English using BAVGROUND, a multiple-choice benchmark, where 206 source questions are aligned across all three languages. Across 14 open-weight 7B--10B instruction models, we compare BF16 with 8-bit GPTQ and two 4-bit settings, GPTQ and AWQ. Eight-bit GPTQ remains close to BF16 and largely preserves the relative behaviour of the three languages, while 4-bit quantisation was found to be much less stable. The two 4-bit methods reduce average accuracy by about 1.4--1.5 percentage points and change 11.9--16.0% of BF16 decisions, with changes concentrated on examples where the BF16 model is already uncertain. This instability does not translate into a consistent Bavarian disadvantage. Although Bavarian, a low-resource dialect, has lower baseline accuracy than German and English, the language most affected at 4 bits varies across models and quantisation methods. Calibration further shapes these cross-language effects: the relative Bavarian--German effect changes with calibration language, while changing the calibration source has little average effect on GPTQ-4 but can affect AWQ-4 much more strongly. Free-form evaluation on five models further shows that 4-bit compression can degrade generated responses even in settings where multiple-choice accuracy changes only modestly, while 8-bit GPTQ remains comparatively stable. Overall, our results show that quantisation robustness for regional language varieties depends on the model, quantisation method, calibration data, and evaluation setting, and cannot be measured by aggregate multilingual accuracy alone.

Do Factuality Methods Make LLMs More Factual? Reproducibility and Fair Comparison
事实性方法会让LLM更具事实性吗？可复现性与公平比较
Pratuat Amatya, Vinay Setty, V Venktesh, Avishek Anand
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large Language Models (LLMs) are aligned to human preferences, after pre-training and supervised fine-tuning steps. However, standard RL alignment steps such as RLHF do not focus on factuality of LLMs, hence they may generate non-factual information, which could result in unintended consequences. In response, a number of factuality alignment approaches have been proposed in the literature which claim to improve factuality of LLMs on their own benchmarks. However, these methods have not been reproduced independently and are also not comparable since each uses a different base model, training data, evaluation set, judge, and metric. In this paper, we present the first independent reproduction of five factuality alignment methods, which span on-policy RL (PPO, GRPO, and Dr.~GRPO) and offline preference optimization (DPO and KTO), and compare them on a common benchmark with common evaluation metrics. We found that none of these methods reproduces in full, and on the common benchmark none of the methods significantly outperforms the base model. On closer inspection, the rewards optimize for format, length, or brevity rather than factuality and relevance, whereas the choice between on-policy and offline training matters little. Furthermore, the evaluation metrics and benchmarks are also part of the problem since they do not measure relevance of text to the prompt. Since there is no ground truth associated with the prompts, the reliance on LLM judges and retrieval for verification also makes the evaluation fragile. We release our code, data, and checkpoints.

The Many Morals of AI: The cautionary bias of North American news narratives in global perspective
AI 的诸多寓意：全球视角下北美新闻叙事的警示性偏向
Andrew Piper, Edie Pearman
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
The stories told about artificial intelligence (AI) play a central role in shaping public understanding, policy debates, and expectations about technological change. News media are especially influential in this process. Using a cross-regional corpus of 12,924 English-language news articles about AI published since 2022, we examine how storytelling about AI varies across media systems in four regions: North America, China, India, and the Middle East. Leveraging large language models, we extract the implicit narrative lessons conveyed by each article---commonly known as story morals---capturing value-laden interpretations that extend beyond thematic content or sentiment. We find that North American AI coverage is uniquely characterized by narratives of caution, while under-emphasizing narratives of innovation and collaboration that are more prevalent elsewhere. However, this pattern is largely explained by a broader regional negativity bias in North American news sentiment, rather than by heightened concern about AI itself. Our findings bring into view the culturally conditioned nature of AI news narratives.

From Hindsight to Foresight: Dissecting Clinical Evidence Acquisition in Large Language Models
从后见之明到前瞻：剖析大型语言模型中的临床证据获取
Ziyang Ling
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) often diagnose full sight, static clinical cases well yet struggle in foresight, dynamic diagnosis. Prior work has improved this limitation by quantifying the information models acquire and by developing stronger follow-up strategies to improve diagnostic accuracy. In contrast, we introduce a distinctive hindsight to systematically dissect why LLMs fail to acquire diagnostically critical evidence, tracing the failure from evidence identification, utilization and downstream diagnostic updating through not only diagnostic accuracy, but also evidence coverage, trajectory dynamics, and elicited probability and information entropy. Starting experiments from the breakdown at the level of capabilities, to the diagnosis of the pre-event state before the evidence arrives, and to the post-event state transition after the evidence arrives, our research has revealed the profound limitations and internal causes existing in the dynamic diagnostic process. At the same time, we have also conducted sufficient verification and generalization experiments to prove that these limitations are widespread. Together, these findings shift the central challenge from whether LLMs possess relevant clinical knowledge to whether they can identify, acquire, and effectively use the right evidence under clinical diagnosis and conduct a more detailed mechanism analysis to identify the exact location of the capability gap.

Abstract
Dialogue and collaborative assistants repeatedly judge what a partner knows, believes, or intends. Typed decision models offer a potential alternative to generative large language models for bounded Theory of Mind (ToM) selection. We present Jev-ToM, comparing five typed decision models and seven generative baselines on 11,117 English text questions from nine ToM benchmarks across six capability groups. TypeSafe Jev reaches 73.2% source-balanced accuracy including native controls and ranks first or second across all six capabilities, leading beliefs, goals/desires/intentions, and emotions. Other typed models show distinct strengths across tasks. Separate resource comparisons suggest that Jev could reduce the cost and waiting time of repeated ToM selection. Candidate expansion reveals distinct selection and output-validity problems. Related-question cues account for most of Jev's downstream gains, with task-dependent effects from predicted states. The findings motivate testing Jev as a ToM selection component in assistants, with task-specific confidence calibration, candidate design, and output validation as integration priorities.

From Relation-Specific Heads to Shared Interventions: Contextual Entrainment in Language Models
从关系特定的注意力头到共享干预：语言模型中的上下文夹带
Jinghan Zheng, Jiajun Shi
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models rely on prompt context to perform in-context learning, follow formats, and adapt to local evidence. This ability, however, also raises a robustness concern: models may reuse irrelevant tokens from earlier context when answering a later query. Prior work identifies this behavior as contextual entrainment and finds attention heads whose ablation reduces it, arguing that these heads are largely task- or relation-specific. But are the mechanisms behind contextual entrainment truly isolated by relation, or do relation-conditioned searches recover reusable components shared across relations? Using factual-distractor relation-completion prompts across 19 lexical-semantic subtypes, we identify attention heads whose ablation reduces entrainment and test how the resulting head sets transfer recovery ability across exact relations, semantic families, and mixed relation distributions. Same-family transfer exceeds different-family transfer, family residuals weaken once globally shared heads are removed, and subtype-specific searches repeatedly rediscover many global heads. Clean-completion and context-use probes further suggest that this shared intervention can reduce harmful copying while preserving ordinary relation completion and simple in-context abilities. Our findings provide a more precise perspective on contextual entrainment and its mitigation: harmful context following is not best addressed by searching for isolated relation-specific circuits, but by using heterogeneous attack prompts to reveal reusable intervention targets whose effects are shaped by semantic relation structure.

Abstract
Pre-trained Large Language Model (LLMs) are effective on many tasks in zero-shot and few-shot settings. For machine translation of low-resource languages, the obvious options are few-shot prompting and fine-tuning on a small parallel set. We ask: what if moderate amounts of low-resource monolingual data are also available? We argue that, rather than continued pretraining, a more effective use of this data is the pre-LLM era technique of back-translation (BT). The current fine-tuned LLM translates monolingual sentences in each language, and the resulting pairs train it in the reverse direction. Updates on the parallel set are interleaved for stable learning. With 1K parallel pairs on Odia and Swahili, BT beats continued pretraining into the low-resource language by 7.7 to 16.4 XCOMET-XXL points in domain. With beam-decoded intermediate translations, it also beats a model with 10 time more parallel data. In-context examples retrieved from the parallel data further improve BT. We also analyze the source, quality and amount of monolingual text. Across five low-resource languages, with Hindi as a high-resource control, and two 3B backbones, BT improves translation into the low-resource language by 16 to 173% XCOMET-XXL over parallel-only fine-tuning. Blind human evaluation on Odia and Sanskrit agrees with the automatic metrics.

TRAP: Tree-Guided Reinforcement-Augmented Probing for Automated LLM Jailbreaking

Mohammad Reza Mirbagheri, Amir Mahdi Sadeghzadeh
cs.CR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Aligned large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak prompts that circumvent their safety guardrails, making the identification of these vulnerabilities important for understanding and mitigating model weaknesses. Existing automated jailbreak methods explore prompt candidates or reuse attack experience, but generally do not learn over a persistent hierarchy that connects related jailbreak strategies, such as role-play, encoding, and obfuscation. This leaves the relationships among reusable strategies underused in guiding adaptive attack selection. We present Tree-Guided Reinforcement-Augmented Probing (TRAP), a hierarchical framework for automated jailbreak strategy discovery that requires only black-box access to the target LLM. TRAP organizes established jailbreak methods and successful attack templates into a semantic strategy tree, connecting broad attack approaches to concrete, reusable strategies. A reinforcement-learning policy based on a tree-structured gradient bandit explores this tree and uses evaluator feedback to update strategy preferences along each selected path. The policy retains these preferences across attack objectives, allowing experience from earlier attempts to guide subsequent strategy selection. Retrieval-augmented prompt construction translates the selected strategy into an attack for the current objective using relevant successful examples. Experiments on AdvBench across seven aligned LLMs show that TRAP outperforms its counterparts on six models under the reported method settings and the common primary evaluator, achieving attack success rates of 45.6% to 97.9% on these models. These findings support hierarchical strategy learning as an effective approach to discovering jailbreak vulnerabilities in aligned LLMs.

VeriRouter: Towards Verifiable LLM Routing

Mengyu Yao, Ziqi Zhang, Shaofei Li, Yifeng Cai, Ding Li, Yao Guo, Ning Luo
cs.CR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) routers are increasingly deployed to optimize quality, latency, and cost through dynamic model selection and request rewriting. However, a compromised router can cause ineligible selection on the control plane, unendorsed rewriting or unfaithful relay on the data plane, undermining LLM routing integrity. We present VeriRouter, a verifiable LLM routing framework. Under an endorsed public context binding a private semantic index and rewrite banks, VeriRouter combines ZK proofs with a provider-issued serving certificate to establish integrity across both planes while keeping the router's private routing assets hidden from clients. For model selection, we design an efficient ZK proof for semantic search. For rewriting, local checks enforce message preservation and additions from committed banks. On real-world workloads, VeriRouter's model-selection and rewrite proofs average 21.92~s and 4.24~s, yielding 1,307$\times$ and 101$\times$ speedups over the fastest completing baselines. Relative to serving without verification, VeriRouter adds only 4.08 s under per-turn selection and 0.11 s under session-pinned selection.

ProtoArena: Can AI Agents Discover and Exploit Real-World Cross-Component Protocol Vulnerabilities?
ProtoArena：AI 智能体能否发现并利用真实世界的跨组件协议漏洞？
Fasheng Miao, Zhaoyu Hu, Xiang Li, Changqing An, Jiutian Zeng, Longtao Huang, Haixin Duan, Jilong Wang
cs.CR · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used for vulnerability analysis, yet existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of exploitation that depends on interactions among network protocol components. Such vulnerabilities arise from inconsistencies in message interpretation, timing, state, or trust assumptions across participants. We introduce ProtoArena, a black-box, multi-component, dynamic benchmark with 80 cross-component vulnerability-exploitation environments spanning 11 protocol and application domains and 7 attack categories. Tasks are primarily informed by published protocol-attack mechanisms. Agents interact with running systems through scoped interfaces to achieve security-effect objectives without target source code. Three information levels assess guided reproduction, exploitation with mechanism and topology context, and effect-directed black-box exploration. A hybrid verifier combines rule-based checks with LLM review of independently collected traffic and logs. We evaluate five LLMs. Claude Opus 4.8 achieves the highest observed success rates: 48.8% under L1 guidance and 12.5% under effect-directed black-box L3. In a separate DNSBomb optimization experiment, it achieves a peak downstream-response to average query-input byte-rate ratio exceeding 171,000 times. The results show that agents can achieve verifiable exploitation effects in some cross-component environments, but success with limited black-box information remains low and varies across domains and attack categories. All experiments use controlled, explicitly authorized targets; they do not test production systems or disclose previously unknown vulnerabilities.

FedGraph: Defending Federated Large Language Model Fine-Tuning Against Backdoor Attacks via Graph-Based Aggregation
FedGraph：通过基于图的聚合防御针对联邦大语言模型微调的后门攻击
Xi Chen, Chunyi Zhou, Rui Zeng, Xiaogang Xu, Zhe Liu, Shouling Ji
cs.CR · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Federated fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) allows multiple clients to collaboratively adapt models without sharing raw data, offering strong privacy benefits. However, this setting is highly vulnerable to backdoor attacks, in which malicious clients manipulate their updates to induce targeted behaviors while maintaining normal performance on benign inputs. In this work, we make a key observation specific to federated LLM fine-tuning: malicious clients tend to exhibit strong consistency in their model updates, whereas benign clients produce more diverse and dispersed updates. This structural difference is not well captured by existing defense methods, which typically rely on direct anomaly detection in high-dimensional parameter space and therefore struggle in the presence of entangled LLM updates. Motivated by this observation, we propose FedGraph, a graph-based aggregation framework that explicitly models relationships among client updates. By representing clients as nodes in a dynamically constructed graph and extracting structural features that characterize their relative positions and interactions, FedGraph derives compact client representations that effectively separate malicious and benign behaviors. These representations are then used to identify and suppress malicious contributions during aggregation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedGraph significantly improves backdoor defense. It consistently reduces attack success rates to below 10% while achieving high detection accuracy (95.5% on average) and a low false positive rate (2.33%), substantially outperforming existing federated learning defenses.

大语言模型（LLMs）的联邦微调允许多个客户端在不共享原始数据的情况下协作适配模型，提供强大的隐私优势。然而，这种设置极易受到后门攻击，其中恶意客户端操纵其更新以诱发目标行为，同时在良性输入上保持正常性能。在这项工作中，我们针对联邦LLM微调做出一个关键观察：恶意客户端在其模型更新中往往表现出很强的一致性，而良性客户端产生更多样且更分散的更新。这种结构性差异未被现有防御方法很好地捕获，这些方法通常依赖高维参数空间中的直接异常检测，因此在存在纠缠的LLM更新时表现不佳。受这一观察启发，我们提出FedGraph，一个基于图的聚合框架，它显式地建模客户端更新之间的关系。通过将客户端表示为动态构建图中的节点，并提取刻画其相对位置和交互的结构特征，FedGraph推导出紧凑的客户端表示，从而有效区分恶意和良性行为。然后，这些表示被用于在聚合过程中识别并抑制恶意贡献。大量实验表明，FedGraph显著改进了后门防御。它持续将攻击成功率降低到10%以下，同时实现高检测准确率（平均95.5%）和低假阳性率（2.33%），显著优于现有的联邦学习防御。

Kairos: Transactional Security Enforcement at the System Boundary for LLM Agents
Kairos：面向 LLM 智能体的系统边界处事务性安全强制执行
Kristoffer Hempel, Nils Loose, Lorenzo Cavallaro, Thomas Eisenbarth
cs.CR · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming an integral part of the software development lifecycle, and the capabilities granted to them allow an agent to act with the user's authority on any resource it can access. The reach that gives an agent its utility is equally available to an attacker who can steer it. Anything an agent ingests can carry an injected instruction, and since the model does not reliably distinguish instructions from data, indirect prompt injection should be mitigated by mediating the effects the agent produces. Such mediation faces a structural difficulty. Legitimate work and the first step of an attack often look alike when an individual action is observed, and what separates them lies later in the trace, so a monitor limited to allow and deny is forced to decide before the evidence accumulates. We present Kairos, a reference monitor at the isolation boundary of an unmodified, opaque agent, where a tool call, a shell command, and a script the agent writes all cross the boundary as the same file and network operations, so that confinement holds regardless of the agent's behavior. A declarative policy that states which sources are trusted decides most effects deterministically and defers the rest, which are held while the agent continues speculatively. A decision oracle with bounded authority, such as a language model or a human, releases or refuses each deferred effect on the trace. Across three benchmarks and three agent models, Kairos outperforms existing defenses in the trade-off between attack success and utility. In particular, on AgentDojo, it reduces attack success from 47.0\% to 2.7\% while its benign utility stays at the level of the undefended agent.

大型语言模型（LLM）智能体正成为软件开发生命周期中不可或缺的一部分，赋予它们的能力使智能体能够以用户的权限对其可访问的任何资源采取行动。赋予智能体实用性的这种触达范围也同样可为能够操纵它的攻击者所用。智能体摄入的任何内容都可能携带注入的指令，而由于模型不能可靠地区分指令与数据，间接提示注入应通过调控智能体所产生的效果来缓解。这种调控面临一个结构性困难。当观察单个动作时，合法工作与攻击的第一步常常看起来相似，而区分它们的东西位于轨迹中的更晚处，因此仅限于允许和拒绝的监视器被迫在证据积累之前做出决定。我们提出 Kairos，一个位于未修改且不透明智能体的隔离边界处的引用监视器，在那里，工具调用、shell 命令以及智能体编写的脚本都以相同的文件和网络操作跨越该边界，因此无论智能体的行为如何，隔离约束都能成立。一个声明式策略说明哪些来源是可信的，确定性地决定大多数效果，并推迟其余效果；其余效果在智能体继续推测性运行时被保持。一个具有受限权限的决策预言机，例如语言模型或人类，基于轨迹释放或拒绝每个被推迟的效果。在三个基准和三个智能体模型上，Kairos 在攻击成功与效用之间的权衡方面优于现有防御。特别地，在 AgentDojo 上，它将攻击成功率从 47.0\% 降低到 2.7\%，同时其良性效用保持在未防御智能体的水平。

Prompt-Segmentation Meets ROI Encryption: Fine-Grained Video Protection Based on Diffusion Isolation
提示分割遇上 ROI 加密：基于扩散隔离的细粒度视频保护
Xiang Zhang, Haoyan Lu, Ziqiang Li, Ziwen He, Zhenshan Tan, Fei Peng, Zhangjie Fu
cs.CR
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Region-of-interest (ROI) selective encryption in H.265/HEVC aims to protect sensitive content while preserving the utility of non-ROI regions. Existing coding-unit (CU)-level approaches still suffer from substantial encryption redundancy for two reasons. First, existing approaches map object-detection bounding boxes to CUs, producing regular rectangular regions, which poorly match the shape of irregular ROI boundaries, such as facial contours. Second, their coding-tree-unit (CTU)-based diffusion isolation expands the protected footprint in fixed $64\times64$ blocks, causing encryption-induced distortion to spread over a large number of non-ROI pixels. To address the aforementioned shortcomings, we propose a prompt segmentation-guided CU-level ROI encryption algorithm, which mainly consists of two core components. The first component is a prompt segmentation-guided fine-grained ROI encryption pipeline. It maps pixel-level ROI masks to CUs according to an ROI-overlap threshold, refines boundary CUs to $8\times8$ granularity, and applies format-compliant encryption to multiple syntax elements in the mapped ROI CUs. The second is a dual diffusion isolation strategy to address the encryption diffusion problem. For spatial isolation, the encoder refines non-ROI boundary regions into $8\times8$ CUs and uses PCM mode to bypass intra-frame prediction. For temporal isolation, it removes motion-vector candidates whose reference blocks overlap ROI CUs. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method generates encryption regions that more closely match irregular ROI boundaries, effectively confines distortion to the ROI.

H.265/HEVC 中的感兴趣区域（ROI）选择性加密旨在保护敏感内容，同时保留非 ROI 区域的可用性。现有的编码单元（CU）级方法仍然因两个原因而存在大量加密冗余。首先，现有方法将目标检测边界框映射到 CU，产生规则的矩形区域，而这些区域难以匹配不规则 ROI 边界的形状，例如面部轮廓。其次，其基于编码树单元（CTU）的扩散隔离会以固定的 $64\times64$ 块扩大受保护范围，导致加密引起的失真扩散到大量非 ROI 像素上。为了解决上述缺点，我们提出了一种提示分割引导的 CU 级 ROI 加密算法，其主要由两个核心组件组成。第一个组件是提示分割引导的细粒度 ROI 加密流水线。它根据 ROI 重叠阈值将像素级 ROI 掩码映射到 CU，将边界 CU 细化到 $8\times8$ 粒度，并对映射后的 ROI CU 中的多个语法元素应用格式兼容加密。第二个是一种双重扩散隔离策略，用于解决加密扩散问题。对于空间隔离，编码器将非 ROI 边界区域细化为 $8\times8$ CU，并使用 PCM 模式绕过帧内预测。对于时间隔离，它移除参考块与 ROI CU 重叠的运动矢量候选。实验结果表明，所提出的方法生成的加密区域更接近不规则 ROI 边界，并有效地将失真限制在 ROI 内。

FlashVSR+: Efficient Video Super-Resolution via Hybrid Attention and Reward-Yield Distribution Matching
FlashVSR+：通过混合注意力与奖励产出分布匹配实现高效视频超分辨率
Ruchang Yao, Shi Guo, Junhao Zhuang, Mingde Yao, Xin Cai, Jiahao Zhan, Bin Fu, Xinyuan Chen, Yu Qiao, Tianfan Xue
cs.CV · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Recent video super-resolution (VSR) models achieve efficient one-step generation through diffusion distillation. However, high-resolution inference remains costly, and distilled models are difficult to align with human preferences. These challenges call for improvements in both model architecture and training strategy. We present \textbf{FlashVSR+} to address both limitations. On the architecture side, we introduce hybrid attention based on the strong locality observed in pretrained VSR models, while retaining sparse global interaction for long-range consistency. It achieves up to $2\times$ DiT speedup and 45\% lower peak memory, enabling spatially untiled 4K VSR on a single 24GB RTX 4090. On the training side, we propose Reward-Yield Distribution Matching Distillation (Ry-DMD) for preference-aligned one-step generation. Ry-DMD uses reward-weighted teacher rollouts to incorporate black-box rewards into distribution matching, without backpropagating through the reward model. We further show that Ry-DMD generalizes beyond VSR to T2I generation. Together, FlashVSR+ delivers stronger restoration quality and substantially improves high-resolution efficiency, with consistent gains in user preference. We release our code, models, and training data at \href{https://www.flashvsr.tech}{\textcolor{FlashBlue}{\textbf{www.flashvsr.tech}}}.

QK-Edit: Revisiting Attention-based Injection in MM-DiT for Image and Video Editing
QK-Edit：重新审视 MM-DiT 中用于图像和视频编辑的基于注意力的注入
Tiancheng Shen, Zilong Huang, Xiangtai Li, Zhijie Lin, Jiyang Liu, Yitong Wang, Jiashi Feng, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Jun Hao Liew
cs.CV · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Multimodal Diffusion Transformers (MM-DiTs) have recently emerged as a powerful framework for unified text-vision synthesis, surpassing traditional U-Net architectures in generative tasks. One key innovation lies in its Multimodal Self-Attention (MM-SA) interaction, where image and text tokens are concatenated and processed via self-attention. However, this mechanism poses significant challenges for editing, rendering conventional U-Net-based attention manipulation methods ineffective. To address this limitation, we propose QK-Edit, a training-free framework that exploits the unique attention dynamics of MM-DiTs for precise text-guided image and video editing. By introducing a novel query-key manipulation strategy, our method isolates and adjusts critical attention components to achieve an optimal balance between prompt fidelity and structural consistency. This enables seamless edits across various tasks, including object addition, object removal, object replacement, changing background, changing material, changing color, and style transformation. Notably, it can be easily implemented with feature replacement in inference. QK-Edit demonstrates superior editing performance on state-of-the-art models, such as FLUX and HunyuanVideo, effectively bridging the gap between generative power and editable flexibility in MM-DiTs, and paving the way for scalable multimodal content creation.

多模态扩散 Transformer（MM-DiT）最近已成为统一文本-视觉合成的强大框架，在生成任务中超越了传统的 U-Net 架构。其中一项关键创新在于其多模态自注意力（MM-SA）交互，其中图像和文本 token 被拼接起来并通过自注意力进行处理。然而，这种机制给编辑带来了重大挑战，使得传统的基于 U-Net 的注意力操控方法失效。为解决这一局限，我们提出 QK-Edit，一个无需训练的框架，它利用 MM-DiT 独特的注意力动态来实现精确的文本引导图像和视频编辑。通过引入一种新颖的查询-键操控策略，我们的方法分离并调整关键的注意力组件，以在提示保真度与结构一致性之间实现最优平衡。这使得跨多种任务的无缝编辑成为可能，包括对象添加、对象移除、对象替换、更改背景、更改材质、更改颜色以及风格转换。值得注意的是，它可以在推理中通过特征替换轻松实现。QK-Edit 在 FLUX 和 HunyuanVideo 等最先进的模型上展现出更优的编辑性能，有效弥合了 MM-DiT 中生成能力与可编辑灵活性之间的差距，并为可扩展的多模态内容创作铺平了道路。

LinMorph: Learning to Morph Weights for Efficient Video DiT Linearization
LinMorph：学习形变权重以实现高效视频 DiT 线性化
Lingyi Long, Congyue Zhao, Xiaoou Li, Yanmin Qian, Tao Huang
cs.CV · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Post-hoc linearization is an attractive way to accelerate pretrained Video Diffusion Transformers (Video DiTs), yet existing methods largely treat the quality loss induced by attention replacement as a recovery problem. We show that a more fundamental bottleneck lies upstream: \emph{initialization}. Random initialization discards pretrained knowledge, whereas manual weight reuse transfers it through rigid and incomplete source--target correspondences. We introduce \textbf{LinMorph}, which recasts Video DiT linearization as a learnable softmax-to-linear weight transformation problem. Instead of copying predefined counterparts, LinMorph learns a cross-parameter morphism that lets each target Gated DeltaNet (GDN) parameter draw jointly from pretrained query, key, value, and output projections, including for parameters with no direct softmax counterpart. A single morphism is shared across layers and learned through local teacher alignment, while producing layer-specific initializations from their respective pretrained weights. The resulting weights are then materialized as independent GDN modules for progressive distillation and joint recovery.Since the morphism operates in weight space rather than token space, it can be learned on short, low-resolution clips and directly reused at larger video scales. Across pretrained Video DiTs, LinMorph enables markedly faster recovery and better final generation quality than random initialization and heuristic weight reuse. Results show that efficient linearization depends not only on how a converted model is recovered, but critically on how pretrained knowledge is transferred before recovery. Project page: https://lonelyling.github.io/LinMorph.

事后线性化是加速预训练 Video Diffusion Transformers（Video DiT）的一种有吸引力的方法，然而现有方法在很大程度上将由注意力替换引起的质量损失视为一个恢复问题。我们表明，更根本的瓶颈位于上游：\emph{初始化}。随机初始化丢弃了预训练知识，而手动权重复用则通过僵化且不完整的源--目标对应关系来传递它。我们引入 \textbf{LinMorph}，它将 Video DiT 线性化重新表述为一个可学习的 softmax 到线性权重变换问题。LinMorph 不是复制预定义的对应项，而是学习一种跨参数形变映射，使每个目标 Gated DeltaNet（GDN）参数能够联合地从预训练的 query、key、value 和 output 投影中获取，包括那些没有直接 softmax 对应项的参数。单个形变映射在各层之间共享，并通过局部教师对齐来学习，同时从各层各自的预训练权重产生层特定的初始化。所得权重随后被具体化为独立的 GDN 模块，用于渐进式蒸馏和联合恢复。由于该形变映射作用于权重空间而非 token 空间，它可以在短时长、低分辨率片段上学习，并直接复用于更大的视频尺度。在各类预训练 Video DiT 上，LinMorph 相比随机初始化和启发式权重复用，能够实现显著更快的恢复和更好的最终生成质量。结果表明，高效线性化不仅取决于转换后的模型如何被恢复，而且关键取决于预训练知识在恢复之前如何被迁移。项目页面：https://lonelyling.github.io/LinMorph.

H-DDCM: Hadamard Codebooks for Fast Generative Image and Video Compression
H-DDCM：用于快速生成式图像与视频压缩的 Hadamard 码本
Or Ronai, Vladimir Kulikov, Tomer Michaeli
cs.CV · cs.AI · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Training-free diffusion-based compression methods repurpose the generative priors of a diffusion or a flow model to compress data without retraining them as task-specific codecs. Recent codebook-based approaches such as Turbo-DDCM achieve strong perceptual quality at ultra-low bitrates, but their reliance on dense Gaussian codebooks remains costly in both memory and computation, and scales poorly with the large latent dimensions of modern image and video generators. Their combinatorial bitstream encoding further becomes computationally heavy at this scale. We introduce H-DDCM, a scalable generative compression framework that replaces Gaussian codebooks with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries. The fast Walsh-Hadamard transform allows for implicitly synthesizing full-dimensional dictionaries with $O(d \log d)$ compute for projection and reconstruction and $O(d)$ memory, without materializing the full-dimensional dictionary. We further introduce an efficient table-free lexicographic coding scheme that makes combinatorial encoding practical at larger dimensions. Beyond images, we adapt the framework to an autoregressive video flow model and develop a streaming compression scheme that periodically re-encodes recently reconstructed frames into a fresh KV-cache prefix, preserving temporal context across segments at no additional transmitted bits. This enables long-form, close to real-time generative video compression on a single GPU. Across image and video benchmarks, H-DDCM achieves competitive rate-distortion-perception performance while substantially reducing the memory and computational overhead of codebook-based training-free generative compression.

Simplifying and Improving On-Policy Distillation for Few-Step Diffusion
简化和改进面向少步扩散的同策略蒸馏
Jiawei Zhang, Ziyu Wan, Nanye Ma, Long Zhao, Dong Chen, Hongyu Liu, Qifeng Chen, Dongdong Chen
cs.CV · cs.LG · eess.IV
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Few-step distillation reduces the sampling cost of diffusion and flow models, but existing approaches often require auxiliary score models or specialized architectures. We show that simple on-policy velocity regression already provides a strong foundation for 4-NFE generation. To represent teacher velocity variation within each coarse transition, we introduce Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that separates local corrections from the student's interval-mean prediction. We further repel the student from weaker teacher predictions, providing a lightweight mechanism for avoiding undesirable modes. The resulting framework, Simplified Matching Distillation (SMD), remains entirely regression-based, requires neither online score estimation nor adversarial training, and leaves the deployed generator unchanged. We evaluate SMD on image generation and editing, 3D generation, video synthesis, and joint audio--video generation, scaling to 33 billion parameters. At 4-NFE, SMD outperforms strong few-step baselines and surpasses multi-step teachers on several benchmarks. It also supports cross-model, multi-teacher, and causal-video distillation.

EgoOmniWorld: Unifying Egocentric Understanding via Ego-Action-World Interactions
EgoOmniWorld：通过自我-动作-世界交互统一自我中心理解
Songruo Chen, Yuqian Fu, Yu Li, Mingkang Dong, Sifan Zhou, Bin Ren, Xu Zheng, Tianwen Qian, Mohamed Elhoseiny, Yanwei Fu
cs.CV · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Egocentric video understanding spans diverse capabilities, modalities, and evaluation formats, yet these are often studied in isolation despite their tight coupling in real-world interaction. We propose the Ego-Action-World interaction loop as a unifying principle: the wearer perceives the world, forms goals, acts, changes the world, and uses feedback to guide subsequent behavior. Based on this view, we introduce EgoOmniWorld, a benchmark organized around four complementary interaction structures: Node captures ego, action, and world states; Edge captures directed relations among them; Chain captures linked dependencies; and Loop captures feedback-closed interactions. We develop an interaction-first, evidence-grounded data pipeline that extracts structured interactions from egocentric videos, grounds them in visual and auditory evidence, and generates questions according to their interaction structure. Required modalities and single- or multi-turn formats follow naturally from the supporting evidence and dependencies. EgoOmniWorld contains 24,166 QA groups, including 20,284 training and 3,882 test samples. Experiments on representative open- and closed-source multimodal large language models reveal substantial and uneven limitations across interaction structures. Models trained on EgoOmniWorld improve in-domain interaction understanding and generalize to existing egocentric benchmarks. EgoOmniWorld provides a unified foundation for evaluating and advancing egocentric video understanding. Data, code, and models will be released.

自我中心视频理解涵盖多样的能力、模态和评估格式，然而尽管它们在现实世界交互中紧密耦合，这些方面却常常被孤立地研究。我们提出自我-动作-世界交互循环作为统一原则：穿戴者感知世界、形成目标、采取行动、改变世界，并利用反馈来指导后续行为。基于这一观点，我们提出 EgoOmniWorld，一个围绕四种互补交互结构组织的基准：Node 捕获自我状态、动作状态和世界状态；Edge 捕获它们之间的有向关系；Chain 捕获链接的依赖关系；Loop 捕获反馈闭环交互。我们开发了一条交互优先、基于证据的数据流水线，它从自我中心视频中提取结构化交互，将它们建立在视觉和听觉证据之上，并根据其交互结构生成问题。所需模态以及单轮或多轮格式自然地源自支撑证据和依赖关系。EgoOmniWorld 包含 24,166 个 QA 组，其中包括 20,284 个训练样本和 3,882 个测试样本。在代表性开源和闭源多模态大语言模型上的实验揭示了跨交互结构存在显著且不均衡的局限。在 EgoOmniWorld 上训练的模型提升了领域内交互理解，并能泛化到现有的自我中心基准。EgoOmniWorld 为评估和推进自我中心视频理解提供了统一基础。数据、代码和模型将会发布。

cs.AI / 69 / 2610.18604
LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
LLM2R：从大型语言模型到三维重装配器
Zhouhan Zhong, Qiuhong Shen, Xingyi Yang, Jinyi Xu, Xinchao Wang
cs.CV · cs.AI · cs.RO
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
3D part assembly aims to reconstruct a complete shape from a set of unassembled parts by predicting a rigid SE(3) transformation for each part. Because the placement of a part is rarely determined by its own geometry, the task demands reasoning over the entire part set, and existing methods, which rely on pairwise relations or iterative generation and verification, scale poorly to objects with many parts. We present LLM2R, which casts part assembly as sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only large language model (LLM): a Point-BERT encoder and a Q-Former compress each part into a block of geometric tokens, the blocks of all parts are concatenated, and a causal LLM adapted with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) processes the sequence in one forward pass. Causal attention, however, lets the hidden states of a part observe only the parts that precede it. LLM2R therefore appends a block of learnable summary tokens after the last part: these tokens follow every part, so their states aggregate the whole assembly at a constant token cost, and a part-aware pose head fuses each part's states with them before predicting its rotation and translation. One architecture thus handles semantic and geometric assembly and predicts all poses in a single non-autoregressive pass. LLM2R achieves the highest part accuracy and success rate on all three PartNet categories, the best rotation error, translation error, and part accuracy on PartNeXt, and the lowest translation error and fastest inference on Breaking Bad, where only a fracture-specialized method is more accurate. Its advantage grows with the number of parts: at 100 parts it exceeds GARF by 33.5 points in part accuracy on Breaking Bad and Assembler by 29.1 points on PartNet, and it transfers zero-shot to unseen categories with more than 16 points higher part accuracy than the strongest of three baselines.
Chinese Translation
三维部件装配旨在通过为每个部件预测一个刚性 SE(3) 变换，从一组未装配的部件中重建一个完整形状。由于一个部件的放置位置很少由其自身几何形状决定，该任务要求对整个部件集合进行推理，而现有方法依赖于成对关系或迭代生成与验证，难以扩展到具有许多部件的物体。我们提出 LLM2R，它将部件装配转化为使用预训练仅解码器大型语言模型（LLM）的序列建模：Point-BERT 编码器和 Q-Former 将每个部件压缩为一个几何 token 块，所有部件的块被拼接起来，而一个通过低秩适配（LoRA）适配的因果 LLM 在一次前向传播中处理该序列。然而，因果注意力使一个部件的隐藏状态只能观察到位于它之前的部件。因此，LLM2R 在最后一个部件之后追加一个可学习的摘要 token 块：这些 token 排在每个部件之后，因此它们的状态以恒定的 token 开销聚合整个装配，而一个部件感知的位姿头在预测每个部件的旋转和平移之前，将其状态与这些摘要 token 的状态融合。因此，一个架构即可处理语义装配和几何装配，并在单次非自回归前向传播中预测所有位姿。LLM2R 在全部三个 PartNet 类别上取得了最高的部件准确率和成功率，在 PartNeXt 上取得了最佳的旋转误差、平移误差和部件准确率，并在 Breaking Bad 上取得了最低的平移误差和最快的推理速度；在 Breaking Bad 上，只有一种断裂专用方法更准确。其优势随着部件数量的增加而增长：在 100 个部件时，它在 Breaking Bad 上的部件准确率比 GARF 高 33.5 个百分点，在 PartNet 上比 Assembler 高 29.1 个百分点，并且它以零样本方式迁移到未见类别，其部件准确率比三个基线中最强的方法高出 16 个点以上。

AIRRI: Towards a Human-Readable, Machine-Resistant Reading Interface
AIRRI：迈向人类可读、抗机器的阅读界面
Emory Salaun, Syed Ayon, Kaleel Mahmood, Shaun Wallace
cs.CV · cs.HC · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
The rapid advancement of image-to-text extraction systems and large language models (LLMs) poses new challenges for educational assessment by making assignment materials easy to transcribe and solve with minimal human effort. To address this problem, we present AIRRI (Artificial Intelligence Resilient Reading Interface), a framework for generating machine-resistant educational content, a dataset of higher-education assignments for evaluation, and an initial evaluation of the human readability of AIRRI machine-resistant text designs. AIRRI employs two categories of machine-resistance techniques. First, AIRRI applies image transformations including character spacing, word spacing, line spacing, character opacity variation, stripe overlays, and image noise. Second, AIRRI applies decision-based adversarial attacks: RayS, SurFree, and ADBA. We evaluate AIRRI against three image-to-text systems: Tesseract, EasyOCR, and the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our results show that AIRRI substantially degrades automated text extraction performance. AIRRI increased character error rates for EasyOCR (6.9% to 55.9%), Tesseract (2.3% to 100.0%), and GOT-OCR2 (30.7% to 48.1%). Word error rates increased for EasyOCR (24.9% to 96.7%) and Tesseract (10.7% to 100.0%). Among the evaluated decision-based attacks, ADBA consistently produced the largest degradation in image-to-text performance, while RayS and SurFree produced more moderate reductions. EasyOCR and Tesseract were generally more susceptible to both image-based and adversarial perturbations than the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our findings suggest that AIRRI can significantly reduce the reliability of image-to-text-to-LLM workflows, increasing the effort required for AI-assisted assignment completion.

图像到文本提取系统和大语言模型（LLMs）的快速发展，使作业材料能够以极少的人工投入被轻松转录和解决，从而给教育评估带来了新的挑战。为解决这一问题，我们提出 AIRRI（Artificial Intelligence Resilient Reading Interface，人工智能韧性阅读界面），一个用于生成抗机器教育内容的框架、一个用于评估的高等教育作业数据集，以及对 AIRRI 抗机器文本设计的人类可读性的初步评估。AIRRI 采用两类抗机器技术。首先，AIRRI 应用图像变换，包括字符间距、单词间距、行间距、字符不透明度变化、条纹叠加和图像噪声。其次，AIRRI 应用基于决策的对抗攻击：RayS、SurFree 和 ADBA。我们针对三种图像到文本系统评估 AIRRI：Tesseract、EasyOCR 和基于 Transformer 的 GOT-OCR2 模型。我们的结果表明，AIRRI 显著降低了自动文本提取性能。AIRRI 提高了 EasyOCR（6.9% 至 55.9%）、Tesseract（2.3% 至 100.0%）和 GOT-OCR2（30.7% 至 48.1%）的字符错误率。EasyOCR（24.9% 至 96.7%）和 Tesseract（10.7% 至 100.0%）的单词错误率上升。在所评估的基于决策的攻击中，ADBA 始终对图像到文本性能产生最大的降低，而 RayS 和 SurFree 产生的降低较为温和。与基于 Transformer 的 GOT-OCR2 模型相比，EasyOCR 和 Tesseract 通常更容易受到基于图像的扰动和对抗性扰动的影响。我们的发现表明，AIRRI 可以显著降低图像到文本再到 LLM 工作流的可靠性，增加 AI 辅助完成作业所需的投入。

OmniCompass: A Holistic Benchmark for Omni-Modal Video Grounding and Understanding
OmniCompass：面向全模态视频定位与理解的综合性基准
Xuyang Liu, Shihao Wang, Xinyu Wei, Minghan Li, Zeqing Wang, Zuhao Yang, Zichen Wen, Lei Zhang
cs.CV · cs.CL · cs.MM
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
With the rapid development of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), evaluating their video understanding capabilities has become increasingly important. Existing video understanding benchmarks cover only part of the evaluation dimensions, limiting systematic diagnosis of omni-modal video understanding. We introduce OmniCompass, a holistic benchmark for omni-modal video grounding and understanding. OmniCompass defines two evaluation tracks: OmniCompass-VL assesses vision-language models on tasks requiring visual evidence, while OmniCompass-AV assesses omni-modal models on tasks requiring joint audio-visual evidence. Each track includes three complementary tasks: temporal grounding (TG), spatial grounding (SG), and question answering (QA), assessing when a referenced target appears, where it is, and what happens. QA covers five perception and three reasoning categories in OmniCompass-VL, and three perception and two reasoning categories in OmniCompass-AV. OmniCompass-VL contains 820 videos and 2,460 instances across domains and three duration types: short, medium, and long. A narrative- and audio-rich subset forms OmniCompass-AV with 240 videos and 720 instances. Each instance is evaluated under two paired settings: text-only and text+image, specifying the same target through text and visual-language guidance. All instances are manually annotated with multi-round quality verification. Evaluations of 50 MLLMs show that open-source models still lag behind proprietary counterparts, particularly in audio-visual understanding. Precise temporal and spatial grounding remains challenging even for leading models, and their predictions still exhibit inconsistencies across the paired target specifications.

A Global View of How LLMs Value Human Time

cs.CY · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) increasingly act as personal assistants; however, little is known about how they capture national-level preferences on a global scale. Given that "time" is a universal and representative concept, we examine LLMs' time preferences by varying only users' country and measuring the compensation LLMs deem appropriate for a 60-minute appointment delay. We then compare LLMs' responses with GDP per capita on Purchasing Power Parity (GDP_PPP), Mean Income, and a literature-based index (Patience Score). Our results across 193 countries and 5 LLMs demonstrate that people's time across the world is evaluated in noticeably different ways among LLMs, as well as varying levels of robustness under prompt variations. LLMs consistently recommend the highest compensation for Europe, but mostly the lowest for Africa. Based on GDP_PPP, LLMs underestimate the value of time for users living in Asia and South America. These findings indicate that geographical patterns are embedded in LLMs and may translate in different treatment in agentic settings.

cs.LG / 73 / 2610.17214
Density-Matrix Reinforcement Learning
密度矩阵强化学习
Chiuman Ho
cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
What information does a reinforcement learning policy omit? At each state, a standard policy stores one probability per action. It has no place to record how actions relate to each other, such as which pairs go together and which conflict. We ask when this missing structure matters, and we give exact answers. We store the policy at each state as a density matrix, a positive semidefinite, unit-trace matrix borrowed from quantum information theory. We use it here as a purely classical data structure, computed on ordinary classical hardware. The diagonal holds the usual action probabilities. The off-diagonal entries, called coherences, are new parameters. This gives density-matrix reinforcement learning (DMRL). Coherences change outcomes in two settings. First, suppose a policy is regularized toward a coherent reference policy using matrix relative entropy. The optimum then has coherences that no diagonal reference policy produces, and its action probabilities can depend on the reference policy's coherences. This is relevant to fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) with a Kullback--Leibler penalty. Second, suppose the agent chooses a unit-vector action and the reward is a quadratic function of that vector. This could arise when an LLM judge scores a weighted consolidation of reasoning paths, or when coupled robotic sensors each respond to a mix of actions. Then some coherent policies earn strictly more expected reward than every classical policy with the same action probabilities, and we give the margin in closed form. In a two-action example, both policies assign probability $0.5$ to each action, yet the classical one earns expected reward $0$ while the coherent one earns $1$, the maximum. Outside these two settings, DMRL matches or transfers the classical results. This is a theory paper. All results are proved, and we report no empirical evaluation.

强化学习策略遗漏了什么信息？在每个状态，标准策略为每个动作存储一个概率。它没有位置记录动作之间如何彼此关联，例如哪些动作对彼此契合、哪些相互冲突。我们追问这种缺失的结构何时重要，并给出精确答案。我们将每个状态处的策略存储为密度矩阵，即一个借自量子信息论的半正定、迹为1的矩阵。我们在这里将其用作一个纯粹经典的数据结构，并在普通经典硬件上计算。对角线保存通常的动作概率。非对角元素，称为相干项，是新参数。这给出了密度矩阵强化学习（DMRL）。相干项在两种情形下改变结果。首先，假设使用矩阵相对熵将一个策略朝着一个相干参考策略进行正则化。此时最优解具有任何对角参考策略都不会产生的相干项，并且其动作概率可能依赖于参考策略的相干项。这与使用 Kullback--Leibler 惩罚对大语言模型（LLMs）进行微调相关。其次，假设智能体选择一个单位向量动作，并且奖励是该向量的二次函数。这可能出现在一个 LLM 评判器对推理路径的加权整合进行评分时，或者耦合的机器人传感器各自响应动作的混合时。那么，一些相干策略获得的期望奖励严格多于每一个具有相同动作概率的经典策略，并且我们以闭式给出该差距。在一个双动作示例中，两个策略都为每个动作分配概率 $0.5$，但经典策略获得的期望奖励为 $0$，而相干策略获得 $1$，即最大值。在这两种情形之外，DMRL 匹配或迁移了经典结果。这是一篇理论论文。所有结果均已证明，并且我们未报告任何实证评估。

LLM-to-Flow Distillation: Teaching Natural Language Goals to Scientific Generators
LLM-to-Flow 蒸馏：将自然语言目标教授给科学生成器
Riccardo De Santi, Federico Di Gennaro, Angelo Gnazzo, Sophia Tang, Pranam Chatterjee, Fanny Yang, İsmail İlkan Ceylan, Michael M. Bronstein, Andreas Krause
cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Generative discovery in science requires coupling high-level scientific reasoning with the ability to generate samples respecting the structure of a design space. Yet these capabilities remain largely separated: foundation LLMs encode broad chemical and biological knowledge, while domain-specific flow- and diffusion-based generators capture the priors needed to produce valid sequences and geometries. We study how to align such scientific generators to high-level natural-language discovery goals without requiring an explicit proxy reward, which is often unavailable or poorly captured by learned predictors in experimental sciences. We introduce LLM-to-Flow Distillation (LFD), where a frozen LLM acts as an adaptive teacher for a domain-specific generator. Given a goal such as 'generate peptides with promising anticancer activity', the teacher constructs a curriculum of intermediate sub-goals aware of the flow's current capabilities, and progressively directs them toward the original discovery goal. At each round, the LLM judges sampled candidates under the current objective. These judgments induce preferences that are iteratively distilled into the generator through DPO. This procedure provides dense learning signals even when the initial model places negligible probability on designs satisfying the final goal, enabling adaptation toward poorly covered, out-of-distribution regions. Experiments on therapeutic peptides and small-molecule structure design demonstrate that LFD enables a new form of generative control: aligning arbitrary domain-specific scientific generators to scientific discovery tasks expressed via high-level natural-language goals.

COMPASS: Membership Inference Attack Against Vision Large Language Models via Adaptive Noise Calibration
COMPASS：通过自适应噪声校准对视觉大语言模型的成员推断攻击
Damien Lo, Hong Kyu Lee, Ruixuan Liu, Li Xiong
cs.LG · cs.CR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Vision large language models (VLLMs) are deployed in privacy-sensitive domains, raising training-data exposure concerns. Existing gray-box membership inference attacks (MIAs) commonly rely on entropy statistics or generated descriptions, requiring costly generation with limited membership separation. Perturbation-based methods instead measure response changes but focus on large perturbations, leaving VLLM membership behavior under smaller perturbations poorly understood. We systematically characterize VLLM membership behavior under controlled Gaussian perturbations across noise levels at fine resolution. We find that optimal perturbation magnitude and membership-signal direction vary across model-dataset pairs. In many settings, a previously unstudied low-noise regime yields stronger separation than large perturbations, with members exhibiting lower divergence than non-members, reversing the conventional score direction. Other settings retain the conventional direction, demonstrating that neither a fixed perturbation magnitude nor a predetermined score orientation is universally reliable. We propose COMPASS, an adaptive gray-box MIA that calibrates both the perturbation magnitude and membership-score direction using a loosely distribution-matched, known non-member reference set. We instantiate COMPASS using Renyi-normalized KL divergence and Renyi divergence, with max-k aggregation over the most informative image-logit positions. Across LLaVA v1.5-7B, MiniGPT-4, and HuluMed-32B, spanning pretraining, instruction-tuning, and medical-image datasets, COMPASS outperforms baselines. On general-domain data, COMPASS achieves AUCs up to 0.88. On the distribution-matched medical evaluation, it reaches 0.64 AUC, while the strongest baseline remains at chance level. These results establish full-range adaptive perturbation analysis as an effective approach to VLLM membership inference.

JustOPD: On-Policy Distillation from Autoregressive to Diffusion Language Models
JustOPD：从自回归到扩散语言模型的同策略蒸馏
Zikun Zhang, Jiayuan Sheng, David D. Yao, Wenpin Tang
cs.LG
diffusionlarge language model
扩散模型相关
大语言模型相关
Abstract
On-policy distillation (OPD) is a post-training approach for large language models (LLMs) that enables a student model to learn a teacher model's distribution from sequences sampled from the student's own policy. Despite its promising capability, OPD for diffusion language models (DLMs) remains underexplored and existing studies primarily focuses on DLM-to-DLM distillation. The limited availability of strong teacher DLMs and the flexible generation order of DLMs impose additional technical challenges as well. However, it remains unclear how to effectively distill knowledge from a strong autoregressive language model (ARM) into a weaker DLM, given the mismatch between the left-to-right decoding of ARMs and the flexible decoding order of DLMs. Inspired by Ni et al. (2026), we propose JustOPD, an ARM-to-DLM on-policy distillation method that uses autoregressive rollouts during training to align the student's generation process with the ARM teacher's left-to-right decoding. This alignment enables effective distillation from ARM teachers while preserving the DLM's flexible generation-order capability at inference time. Experiments using Qwen3-14B as the teacher and Dream-7B as the student demonstrate that JustOPD consistently improves mathematical reasoning performance over the base DLM across multiple divergence choices.

Cross-View Time-Frequency Diffusion for Extreme-Aware Time-Series Generation
面向极端感知时间序列生成的跨视图时频扩散
Lin Jiang, Rongchao Xu, Guang Wang
cs.LG · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Generating realistic time-series requires faithfully reproducing rare but high-impact extreme events. Existing approaches often rely on specialized representations or extreme-focused training objectives, which may restrict the diversity of captured extremes or compromise overall distributional fidelity. We propose Cross-View Time-Frequency Diffusion (CrossTF), a framework that exploits discrepancies between time- and frequency-view denoisers for extreme-aware time-series generation. Our key empirical finding is extreme-sensitive cross-view asymmetry: moving along the direction connecting the two views' clean-sample estimates substantially changes extreme fidelity while having limited effects on overall generation quality. We further identify a late-stage cross-view window in which this discrepancy stabilizes and cross-view adjustments have a particularly strong effect on extreme fidelity. These findings motivate a staged optimization strategy in CrossTF: after training and freezing both denoisers, it only needs to learn step-specific fusion parameters within this window using an Extreme Value Theory-based objective under an energy-distance constraint. This formulation supports interpolation between and extrapolation beyond the view-specific estimates while limiting degradation in overall generation quality. Extensive experiments on seven real-world datasets against 11 baselines show that CrossTF improves extreme fidelity by 26.1% and overall performance by 7.4% relative to the strongest baselines. These results highlight cross-view discrepancy as an effective basis for low-dimensional optimization in extreme-aware time-series generation.

Reinforcement Learning In Partially Verifiable Environments for Colon Cancer Treatment Planning
Li-Ching Chen, Andrés Franco Valiente, Yuta Ishiyama, Zachary R. Chalmers, William Chen, Kelsey Natsuhara, Taema Brinjikji, Madhumita Sushil, Travis Zack, Julian C. Hong
cs.LG · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Clinical decision-making is a sequential process of information collection, clinical inference, and forecasting under partial observability, often without a uniquely correct treatment decision. Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong medical question-answering capabilities but extending these advances to clinical reasoning remains challenging because many clinical tasks are only partially verifiable. Recent clinical reinforcement learning (RL) work has therefore largely focused on diagnostic endpoints, where correctness can be more directly verified. Oncology treatment decision making is a particularly challenging instance of this problem that extends beyond medical question-answering in which multiple decision trajectories can be clinically defensible for the same partially observed patient state. We formulate oncology treatment planning as an interactive RL problem under partial observability and construct patient-specific, process-aware rewards from decision processes observed in real world clinical records. The agent must learn to sequentially acquire information from a structured patient representation before committing to a first-line treatment recommendation, and is evaluated on information gathering, treatment selection, and reasoning alignment. Using GRPO and GDPO to optimize Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct within this environment, RL substantially improves the base policy beyond frontier model capabilities. The GDPO-trained policy increases Mean@3 scalar clinical reward by $79.60\%$ over base Llama and exceeds GPT-5.2 by $18.82\%$ under the same interactive environment, while reducing query count during training. Overall, our results show that patient-specific, partially verifiable rewards can provide an effective learning signal for interactive clinical RL when both the patient state and the underlying clinical decision process are only partially observed.

Alexander Miasnikov, Ruslan Kabirov, Gleb Molodtsov, Dmitrii Vlashchuk, Vladimir Aletov, Nail Bashirov, Daniil Tikhonov, Maxim Krutikov, Aleksandr Shestakov, Aleksandr Beznosikov

Abstract
Training large language models is constrained by both wall-clock time and memory footprint, and recent matrix-aware optimizers sharpen this tradeoff: Muon can improve optimization but its dense polar update remains expensive. We propose Monarch-Muon, a structured matrix-aware optimizer for weights parameterized by Monarch factors. The resulting structure reduces weights, gradients, and optimizer state, and exposes small independent update subproblems in place of a single dense orthogonalization; we formalize this through a blockwise trust-region interpretation. In quality runs, Monarch-Muon improves over Monarch-AdamW at fixed structure: 3.06 vs. 3.09 in the dense 257M model and 2.68 vs. 2.77 in the 1B MoE model; the two-block MoE variant also matches dense AdamW while using 15% fewer active and 25.4% fewer total parameters. In 6.89B-parameter systems measurements, Monarch-Muon reduces peak memory from 68.9 to 52.9 GB, Muon optimizer state from 14.60 to 6.77 GB, and the Muon optimizer step from 1288 to 304 ms.

Abstract
Active learning changes the representations used to acquire subsequent labels. We study this interaction through Collapse-Based Active Neural Learning (CÆNL), which separates acquisition, Dynamic Collapse Regularization (DCR), and its coefficient policy. DCR penalizes a normalized within-class to between-class scatter residual above a frozen reference, with a separate class-separation safeguard. Fixed, scheduled, deterministic-feedback, and learned-feedback policies apply this objective. The analysis establishes scatter invariances, conditional local descent, and coefficient bounds, and shows why clean geometry alone cannot guarantee input robustness. Six-seed classification comparisons are complemented by a 104-run study with separate control selection and ten-seed evaluations on each of two backbones. At 60% annotations on ImageNet-100, entropy acquisition with DCR and MACC-Lite reaches 73.420 +/- 0.512% accuracy on ResNet-50 and 73.086 +/- 0.397% on ResNet-18 (mean +/- seed SD), exceeding entropy alone by 1.742 and 1.834 percentage points. Both gains survive Holm correction under paired-t and exact sign-flip tests, with unchanged feedback settings across backbones. Independently tuned constants attain slightly higher mean accuracy; the paired comparisons establish neither adaptive superiority nor equivalence. Separate six-seed spectral studies yield a small fixed-regularization C4 loss reduction, worse CIFAR-10 diffusion FID, and inconclusive AudioCaps captioning effects. Earlier classification studies find near-zero AutoAttack accuracy at L-infinity radius 8/255 and no added benefit from learned control. The results support the evaluated combined classification treatment and identify the task dependence of geometry-informed regularization.

Towards Green AI: Evaluating Energy Efficiency for Quantized LLM Inference
迈向绿色 AI：评估量化 LLM 推理的能效
Petar Basta
cs.LG · cs.AI · cs.CY
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
While it is known that quantization of large language models (LLMs) reduces memory usage via lower-bit weights, studies quantifying the resulting impact on energy usage and carbon intensity are scarce. We present the first unified evaluation of weight-only quantization strategies for LLM inference across varying input/output lengths and GPUs, highlighting differences in energy efficiency in addition to accuracy degradation and runtime. We study quantized inference on Llama 2 7B, Phi 3.5 Mini Instruct, OLMo 1B, Qwen 2.5 7B, and Qwen 2.5 14B across GLUE MNLI, MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K datasets, evaluating 10 post-training quantization (PTQ) strategies on NVIDIA H100, A6000, A100, and L4 GPUs. We identify a novel trend showing that quantization techniques tend to exhibit peak energy efficiency relative to full-precision baselines when inputs are sufficiently long and outputs are short. Furthermore, we show that quantization strategies become marginally more energy-efficient relative to full-precision models as batch sizes increase, though gains are modest. Notably, fused-kernel implementations such as EETQ int8 and Bitsandbytes int8 offer the highest energy savings, up to 4x compared to FP32 on short text generation, with negligible accuracy loss. Finally, we observe that energy usage closely tracks runtime on our evaluated benchmarks, indicating that, in practice, latency optimization can serve as a reliable proxy for reducing the environmental footprint of LLM services. We conclude with suggested directions for strategically selecting low-carbon quantization strategies based on specific inference requirements.
