Revisiting the 16x Pretraining Compute Gap between Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models
重新审视扩散语言模型与自回归语言模型之间16倍的预训练计算量差距
Guanghan Wang, Bing He, Zhan Shi, Benoit Dumoulin, Hanqing Lu, Volodymyr Kuleshov
cs.LG · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion language models (DLMs) have attracted wide attention for their fast, parallel decoding, but they are believed to be far less efficient to train than autoregressive language models (ARMs): a widely cited study reports that a DLM needs roughly 16x the training compute of an ARM to match its likelihood, a figure that has made pretraining DLMs from scratch look prohibitive at scale. We find that the methodology behind this figure has fallen out of step with current DLM practice: it scores the model with its evidence lower bound (ELBO) and trains a full-sequence, decoder-only model. We therefore revisit the scaling laws of DLMs, adopting the exact likelihood under the model's own decoding order, block diffusion training, an encoder-decoder architecture, and a sweep over the block sizes used in practice. Under this new protocol, we study across ten model variants, about 1,700 models in total, and find that pretraining DLMs is far cheaper than previously thought. Concretely, scoring with the exact likelihood reduces the compute multiple to 12.8x; block diffusion training and an encoder-decoder architecture further reduce it to 7.8x at block size 32, and smaller block sizes narrow it to 4.6x at block size 8 and 3.0x at block size 4. We complement these scaling analyses with an empirical rule for the optimal decoder depth of encoder-decoder block diffusion, a held-out compute budget beyond the fitting range at which the gap between variants persists, and downstream benchmark results where likelihood improvements carry over to accuracy. Overall, the 16x figure substantially overstates the pretraining cost gap between DLMs and ARMs, and pretraining DLMs from scratch is far more viable than previously assumed.

扩散语言模型（DLMs）因其快速、并行的解码而受到广泛关注，但人们认为它们的训练效率远低于自回归语言模型（ARMs）：一项被广泛引用的研究报告称，一个 DLM 要达到与 ARM 相当的对数似然，所需的训练计算量约为 ARM 的 16 倍，这一数字使得在大规模下从头预训练 DLM 显得代价高不可攀。我们发现，这一数字背后的方法论已与当前 DLM 的实践脱节：它使用证据下界（ELBO）对模型进行评分，并且训练的是全序列的、仅解码器（decoder-only）模型。因此，我们重新审视 DLM 的缩放定律，采用模型自身解码顺序下的精确似然、块扩散训练、编码器-解码器架构，并对实践中使用的块大小进行扫描。在这一新方案下，我们研究了十种模型变体，总计约 1,700 个模型，并发现预训练 DLM 远比此前认为的要便宜。具体而言，使用精确似然评分将计算倍数降至 12.8 倍；块扩散训练与编码器-解码器架构在块大小为 32 时进一步将其降至 7.8 倍，而更小的块大小则在块大小为 8 时将其缩小至 4.6 倍，在块大小为 4 时缩小至 3.0 倍。我们以如下内容补充这些缩放分析：关于编码器-解码器块扩散最优解码器深度的经验性规律、超出拟合范围的留出计算预算（在该预算下各变体之间的差距依然存在），以及下游基准测试结果（其中似然的提升传递到了准确率上）。总体而言，16 倍这一数字大幅高估了 DLM 与 ARM 之间的预训练成本差距，从头预训练 DLM 远比此前假设的更可行。

The Tokens Strike Back: Safety-Aware Denoising with Directional Embedding-based Revision
词元反击：基于方向性嵌入修正的安全感知去噪
Amman Yusuf, Jiwoo Shin, Ruizhi Deng, Heitor Rodrigues Guimarães, Nikita Dvornik, Mijung Park
cs.LG · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
The Safety-Aware Denoiser (SAD) is a recent, training-free, safety-guidance framework for text diffusion models. During inference, SAD steers text samples toward safe regions of the token probability space. In this paper, we propose $\mathit{SADDER}$ (Safety-Aware Denoising with Directional Embedding-based Revision), which improves the safety and quality trade-offs of SAD by exploiting a safety-guidance signal in the embedding (or activation) space for each token position, then updating the token positions using the SAD update rule multiplied by the guidance signal. This multiplication acts as a gating mechanism: tokens with a high unsafe signal are more likely to be modified during inference following the SAD update rule. However, such an update does not automatically preserve the conditional mean, i.e., the denoiser of a fixed target distribution. We therefore theoretically derive new position-wise target distributions for which the modified denoiser is exact. Furthermore, we derive conditions under which the position-wise target distributions match a global target distribution. We test our $\mathit{SADDER}$ method on popular Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs) and Uniform-State Diffusion Models (USDMs) across unsafe continuation and jailbreak settings, and show that $\mathit{SADDER}$ achieves a better balance between safety, generation quality, and inference cost than existing methods.

MissPath-FM: Flow Matching with Structured Priors for Partially Observed Time Series
MissPath-FM：面向部分观测时间序列的结构化先验流匹配
Genpei Zhang
cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Flow matching has emerged as a powerful alternative to diffusion models for generative modeling, but standard conditional flow matching is fundamentally misaligned with partially observed time series: starting from an uninformed Gaussian source forces the model to transport even already-observed entries from noise to the target, wasting capacity on trivially known regions. We propose MissPath-FM, a partial-observation-aware flow matching framework that redesigns the source prior and probability path for incomplete time series. MissPath-FM employs structured source priors (interpolation priors and Gaussian process posterior priors) to initialize the flow close to the observed signal, paired with a missingness-aware smooth path that allocates transport asymmetrically between observed and missing regions. We evaluate systematically across four datasets, four missingness mechanisms (MCAR, block, MNAR, irregular), two missing ratios, and three sequence lengths (T in {24, 48, 96}), totaling 48 settings against eight baselines. MissPath-FM wins 29 of 32 settings at T=48 and 45 of 48 overall (93.8%). Our ablations reveal a regime-dependent design hierarchy in which no single component suffices: under random missingness the source prior yields a large initial gain, but under structured block missingness it can fail entirely and the learned flow becomes indispensable; the missingness-aware path contributes a further 12%-26% across all regimes. Mechanistically, structured priors shorten observed-region transport by up to 15x, concentrating the velocity field on genuinely uncertain entries. Project page: https://zgp110.github.io/misspath-fm/

TSRL: Trigger-based Supervised Reinforcement Learning for Continual Agent Training
TSRL：面向持续智能体训练的基于触发的监督强化学习
Yuqian Fu, Kaiwen Jiang, Zijun Song, Jiawei Wang, Yuanheng Zhu, Dongbin Zhao
cs.LG · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) agents excel at complex, multi-step tasks but suffer from catastrophic forgetting during continual learning--acquiring new skills often degrades previously mastered capabilities. Existing post-training paradigms face a fundamental trade-off: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is sample-efficient but prone to severe forgetting, while Reinforcement Learning (RL) preserves prior capabilities but converges slowly without expert guidance. To bridge this gap, we introduce Trigger-based Supervised Reinforcement Learning (TSRL), a framework that integrates the strengths of both paradigms through an adaptive, state-dependent expert supervision mechanism. TSRL employs RL as the optimization backbone, activating SFT selectively on "hard states" where the policy fails. Theoretically, we show that restricting supervision to failure states derives an upper bound on the cumulative parameter updates, thereby reducing forgetting compared to full SFT. Empirically, TSRL achieves consistent gains across three agent benchmarks (ALFWorld, WebShop, and Deep Search) at both 7B and 32B scales. In continual learning scenarios, our method retains up to 9.6 points more capability on prior tasks than SFT->RL baselines, while matching or exceeding target-task performance.

大型语言模型（LLM）智能体擅长复杂、多步任务，但在持续学习中会遭受灾难性遗忘——习得新技能往往会损害先前已掌握的能力。现有的后训练范式面临一个根本性的权衡：监督微调（SFT）样本效率高，但容易发生严重遗忘，而强化学习（RL）能够保留先有能力，但在没有专家指导时收敛缓慢。为弥合这一差距，我们提出基于触发的监督强化学习（TSRL），这是一个通过自适应、依赖状态的专家监督机制来整合两种范式优势的框架。TSRL 采用 RL 作为优化主干，在策略失败的“困难状态”上有选择地激活 SFT。在理论上，我们表明，将监督限制于失败状态可推导出累积参数更新的上界，从而相较于完整 SFT 减少遗忘。在实证上，TSRL 在三个智能体基准（ALFWorld、WebShop 和 Deep Search）上于 7B 和 32B 规模均取得了一致的提升。在持续学习场景中，我们的方法在先前任务上比 SFT->RL 基线最多多保留 9.6 个点的能力，同时在目标任务性能上持平或超过基线。

CoCA: Criterion-Aware Credit Assignment for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
CoCA：面向基于评分标准的强化学习的准则感知信用分配
Guangcheng Zhu, Yingfan Ma, Xing Zheng, Haobo Wang, Shenzhi Yang, Kai Tang, Zhengqing Zang, Bowen Song, Weiqiang Wang, Gang Chen
cs.LG · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) evaluates responses against explicit criteria to construct rewards, offering a viable way to train large language models on open-ended tasks. However, standard methods compress criterion-level feedback into scalar rewards and assign uniform token advantages, leaving structured rubric supervision underutilized. Recent work seeks finer-grained guidance by treating rubrics as privileged information to derive self-distillation targets, but the resulting learning signal is not grounded in criterion outcomes and can lead to reward degradation. This motivates us to reframe the problem as criterion-aware credit assignment, where privileged rubric information serves as a relevance cue for credit allocation rather than a source of imitation targets. Accordingly, we propose CoCA, which derives criterion-level credits from group-relative outcomes and allocates them across tokens based on criterion-induced distribution shifts, yielding both outcome-grounded and fine-grained learning signals. Empirically, CoCA achieves an average gain of +4.2% over standard rubric-based RL across medicine and science benchmarks, demonstrating more effective learning on open-ended tasks.

基于评分标准的强化学习（RL）根据显式准则评估回答以构建奖励，为在开放式任务上训练大型语言模型提供了一条可行途径。然而，标准方法将准则级反馈压缩为标量奖励，并分配统一的词元优势，使结构化的评分标准监督未被充分利用。近期工作通过将评分标准视为特权信息来推导自蒸馏目标，以寻求更细粒度的指导，但由此产生的学习信号并不以准则结果为根据，并可能导致奖励退化。这促使我们将该问题重新表述为准则感知的信用分配，其中特权评分标准信息作为信用分配的相关性线索，而不是模仿目标的来源。因此，我们提出了 CoCA，它从组相对结果中推导出准则级信用，并基于准则诱导的分布偏移将其分配到各个词元，从而产生既以结果为根据又细粒度的学习信号。在实证上，CoCA 在医学和科学基准上相较于标准基于评分标准的强化学习取得了平均 +4.2% 的提升，表明其在开放式任务上学习更有效。

大语言模型相关
Abstract
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become a principal recipe for improving the reasoning of large language models (LLMs). It rests on the assumption that the checker scoring each response is itself correct. In practice, rule-based checkers reject correct answers in unexpected formats, unit tests accept incorrect programs, and LLM judges can be led to approve empty or adversarial responses. This work surveys 58 studies that measure, analyze, or mitigate such verifier errors. We ask what errors verifiers make, how they affect training, which mitigations work against which errors, and how the findings extend to self-generated, rubric- and judge-based, and verifier-free rewards. The evidence suggests that the structure of an error matters more than its rate. Random errors mostly slow learning, though under a fixed budget or KL regularization they also lower final accuracy. False positives that the policy can learn to trigger can cause plateaus or collapse, sometimes even with a low initial error rate. Whether a verifier wrongly rejects or accepts depends on what it checks and who built it, not on its family. Its errors shift as the policy improves, and most mitigations have been tested against only one kind of error. We compile the findings into comparison tables, reconcile apparent conflicts in the literature, and propose a reporting protocol to make future results comparable.
Chinese Translation
带可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）已成为提升大语言模型（LLM）推理能力的主要方法。它建立在这样一个假设之上：为每个回答打分的检查器本身是正确的。在实践中，基于规则的检查器会拒绝格式出乎意料的正确答案，单元测试会接受错误的程序，而 LLM 评判器可能被诱导去认可空洞或对抗性的回答。本工作综述了 58 项测量、分析或缓解此类验证器错误的研究。我们追问：验证器会犯哪些错误，这些错误如何影响训练，哪些缓解措施对哪些错误有效，以及这些发现如何推广到自生成奖励、基于评分标准与评判器的奖励，以及无验证器的奖励。证据表明，错误的结构比其发生率更重要。随机错误大多只是减慢学习速度，不过在固定预算或 KL 正则化下，它们也会降低最终准确率。策略能够学会触发的假阳性可能导致停滞或崩溃，有时即便初始错误率很低也会如此。一个验证器是错误拒绝还是错误接受，取决于它检查什么以及由谁构建，而不取决于它所属的类别。随着策略的改进，它的错误也会发生变化，而大多数缓解措施只针对一种错误进行过测试。我们将这些发现整理成对比表格，调和文献中表面上的冲突，并提出一套报告规范，以使未来的结果具有可比性。

Agentic-MatriBO: Capability-Compiled Agentic Bayesian Optimization for Materials and Chemical Design
Agentic-MatriBO：面向材料与化学设计的能力编译智能体贝叶斯优化
Yu Zeng, Yuchuan Chen, Ziyue Zhang, Zijian Wei, Yanyi Su, Guojiang Zhao, Hongshuai Wang, Zhifeng Gao
cs.LG · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Materials and chemical optimization must choose the next synthesis, characterization, or high-fidelity simulation from sequential observations under a limited budget. Large language models can use task knowledge to propose adjustments, but composing surrogates, acquisition functions, and search strategies is constrained by compatibility, parameter dependencies, and evidence requirements. We present Agentic-MatriBO, a capability-compiled agentic Bayesian optimization (BO) framework that represents BO components and selection conditions as composable capabilities. A language policy proposes BO recipes and candidate plans; a compiler checks proposals against the registered capability catalog; and a deterministic execution layer validates and commits candidates. Oracle observations are stored in research memory and inform later rounds. We compare Agentic-MatriBO with eight baselines on four offline finite candidate pools---COF, PCE10, Buchwald--Hartwig (BH), and Suzuki--Miyaura---using five seeds per condition; results are reported descriptively. Across the four tasks, Agentic-MatriBO has the best mean endpoint quality after orienting each objective so that higher is better. On COF, it reaches the tabulated optimum in all five seeds both in the end-to-end comparison and after shared initialization, where it also retains an advantage in cumulative quality. Its normalized area under the best-so-far quality curve during the BO stage (nAUC-BO) is substantially higher on COF, near parity with the best baseline on PCE10 and BH, and lower on Suzuki. COF ablations show that removing the capability compiler or evidence gate coincides with lower cumulative quality and fewer exact-optimum hits. The framework provides an inspectable interface for evidence-conditioned BO adaptation.

MMTA: Benchmarking Multimodal Temporal Analysis with Time Series, Text, and Vision
MMTA：以时间序列、文本与视觉对多模态时序分析进行基准测试
Ziyang Zhang, Shenyi Li, Yilin Wang, Ziyun Cui, Bowen Zhou, Wen Wu, Chao Zhang
cs.LG · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Time-series analysis is increasingly studied in multimodal settings, yet most benchmarks pair temporal signals with text or with visualizations derived from the same signal. This leaves open whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can integrate time series with real-world visual evidence. We introduce MMTA (multimodal temporal analysis), a benchmark of tri-modal tasks with diverse cross-modal complementarity patterns among time series, text, and vision. MMTA spans nine domains -- robotics, autonomous driving, human action, manufacturing, AR assistance, healthcare, recommendation, finance, and climate -- under video+TS and image+TS layouts, with a 3,524-sample test split covering classification and forecasting. The benchmark standardizes heterogeneous real-world sources into a shared schema with domain-specific prompts, provenance documentation, and success-weighted metrics that penalize both wrong answers and failed generations. Evaluating eight open-source and proprietary MLLMs reveals a shared bottleneck: representing time series as text creates very long token sequences and weakens fine-grained alignment with visual evidence, especially in long-video settings. We then introduce TimeOmni-v, a multimodal LLM extension with a dedicated time-series encoder, temporal positional alignment, modality-aware token layout, and a forecasting head. TimeOmni-v improves long-video classification and time-series inference efficiency, showing that MMTA not only exposes representation and grounding failures but also motivates targeted model design.

Stein Variational Distributional Reinforcement Learning: Score-Guided Particles for Multivariate Return Distributions
Stein 变分分布强化学习：面向多变量回报分布的分数引导粒子
Manuel Haußmann, Melih Kandemir
cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Decisions that weigh several reward signals against each other require the joint distribution of the return vector. Categorical critics scale exponentially in the reward dimension, and quantiles have no canonical multivariate analogue. Multivariate distributional critics therefore represent each return distribution by M equal-weight particles trained with a discrepancy loss. Beyond their atoms, the particles provide no sampler and cannot resolve events rarer than 1/M. We propose Stein variational distributional RL (SVDRL). Its critic outputs Stein particles, which Stein variational gradient descent transports along a learned score field of the distributional Bellman target. We learn this field by bootstrapped denoising score matching across noise levels and tie it across the Bellman recursion by a consistency loss, which we prove is a non-expansive temporal-difference scheme in score space. The same field certifies the particles. Its reverse-diffusion sampler satisfies a supremal Wasserstein policy-evaluation bound that holds for bounded, possibly multimodal returns. The Stein particles inherit this bound up to a gap that we measure without ground truth, and the sampler answers tail-risk queries below the particle resolution at any sample size. Empirically, SVDRL is more accurate on rare events than particle critics with the same number of particles, and on par on MuJoCo continuous control.

对多个奖励信号进行权衡的决策需要回报向量的联合分布。类别型评论器随奖励维度呈指数增长，而分位数没有规范的多变量对应物。因此，多变量分布评论器用 M 个等权粒子表示每个回报分布，这些粒子通过差异损失训练。除了其原子之外，这些粒子不提供采样器，并且无法分辨比 1/M 更稀有的事件。我们提出 Stein 变分分布强化学习（SVDRL）。它的评论器输出 Stein 粒子，Stein 变分梯度下降将这些粒子沿分布 Bellman 目标的学习到的分数场输运。我们通过在多个噪声水平上的自举去噪分数匹配来学习该场，并通过一致性损失将其在 Bellman 递归中绑定；我们证明该方案是分数空间中的非扩张时序差分方案。同一个场也对这些粒子提供认证。它的反向扩散采样器满足一个上确界 Wasserstein 策略评估界，该界对可能多峰的有界回报成立。Stein 粒子继承该界，最多相差一个我们无需真实值即可测量的间隙；并且该采样器能在任意样本量下回答低于粒子分辨率的尾部风险查询。在经验上，SVDRL 在罕见事件上比具有相同粒子数的粒子评论器更准确，并且在 MuJoCo 连续控制上与之相当。

HaloBlock: Faster and Better Decoding for Diffusion Large Language Models
HaloBlock：面向扩散大型语言模型的更快、更好的解码
Zhaohui Zheng, Chenhang He, Jinrui Zhang, Ming-Ming Cheng, Lei Zhang
cs.LG · cs.AI · cs.CL
diffusionlarge language model
扩散模型相关
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) have attracted increasing research attention due to their bidirectional attention and arbitrary order decoding. However, there are two issues in dLLMs inference: the decoding difficulty is dominated by the tokens on the right side of the block, and the block-wise decoding inherently suffers from boundary contextual discontinuity. To tackle these limitations, we propose HaloBlock, a difficulty-aware adaptive halo mechanism for dLLM inference. We first leverage bidirectional cumulative entropy to characterize block decoding difficulty. Then, based on the bidirectional decoding difficulty, we adaptively allocate bidirectional halo regions on both sides of each block to mitigate boundary contextual discontinuity. The difficulty-aware design of HaloBlock smooths cross-block context propagation and lowers decoding difficulty for hard tokens, yielding better generation quality and faster convergence. Evaluated on LLaDA-8B-Instruct, Dream-7B-Instruct and LLaDA-1.5 across mathematical reasoning and code generation benchmarks, HaloBlock demonstrates consistent accuracy improvements and higher inference efficiency. Source codes are publicly available at https://github.com/PolyU-VCLab/HaloBlock.

BELT : BEhavior-Aligned Low-Rank KV Cache Compression with Learned Top-k Rank Allocation
BELT：行为对齐的低秩 KV 缓存压缩与学习式 Top-k 秩分配
Yaoyang Liu, Shuwei Shen, Jincheng Tang, Jinguang Liu, Jinbao Xue, Hailong Yang, Ke Zhang, Yinjun Wu
cs.LG · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Long-context inference makes the key-value (KV) cache a major memory bottleneck for large language models. We propose BELT, a low-rank KV cache compression framework. Its key-side objective targets attention distributions rather than raw keys or pre-softmax logits, yielding a quadratic surrogate with a closed-form low-rank solution. A learned global rank allocator uses differentiable soft selection during training and hard selection at deployment to meet a user-specified component budget. Experiments demonstrate improved model quality under aggressive compression and increased decoding throughput at comparable accuracy. Evaluated across three LLMs and multiple benchmarks, BELT achieves up to 70% low-rank KV cache compression while outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 23.3 points on LongBench, and up to 17.8x overall KV cache reduction when combined with quantization. With Triton-based GPU kernels and a quantized cache, BELT delivers up to 2.7x speedup for the attention module and 3.3x end-to-end decoding throughput.

Match the Canvas, Not Just the Answer: Predictability-Aware SFT for Diffusion Language Models
匹配画布，而不仅仅是答案：面向扩散语言模型的可预测性感知 SFT
Miao Li, Hanyang Jiang, Hengyu Fu, Baihe Huang, Yating Liu, Yuhang Cai, Changkun Guan, Zhongzhu Chen, Jiecheng Lu, Michael A. Boateng, Pascal Van Hentenryck
cs.LG · cs.AI · cs.CL
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion language models (DLMs) enable flexible parallel generation by resolving tokens according to the model's evolving predictability rather than a fixed left-to-right order. This flexibility, however, introduces training choices absent from standard autoregressive teacher forcing: which reference tokens are visible when a target is supervised and how much generation space is allocated. Standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT) typically makes these choices through random masking, independently of inference. Our analysis shows how this training-inference mismatch can misdirect supervision. Random masking can conceal prediction errors or penalize uncertainty that decoding would otherwise resolve, while the attention-visible input length can change which response formulations the model favors, even when the underlying solution is unchanged. Motivated by these findings, we propose Predictability-Aware Canvas Selection and Supervision (PACS), an SFT method. PACS uses the model's own predictability to select each example's attention-visible input length and supervises reference tokens immediately before their confidence-guided revelation. Across reasoning and code-generation benchmarks, PACS consistently achieves the highest mean accuracy among the compared SFT methods, with gains of up to 12.84 percentage points over vanilla SFT on individual benchmarks. Code will be released upon publication.

FRACTION: Fraud Explanation Generation via Agentic Graph Context Navigation
FRACTION：通过智能体图上下文导航进行欺诈解释生成
Cecelia Soh, Jun Hu, Yuan Li, Cheng Chen, Hui Liu, Yanjia Zhu, Hao He, Bryan Hooi, Bingsheng He
cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Graph fraud explanation generation emerges as an important task, which requires jointly leveraging graph structure and content information to produce human-readable explanations for a given risk label. An intuitive approach is to adapt existing graph-enhanced large language models (LLMs), which inject graph structure into LLMs via graph-conditioned instruction tuning or structure-aware embeddings. However, existing methods face two key challenges in graph fraud explanation generation: a lack of evaluation protocols tailored to explanation quality, and a mismatch between the granularity of graph information they provide and what explanation generation requires. In this paper, we propose FRaud Explanation Generation via Agentic Graph Context NavigaTION (FRACTION), a framework for graph fraud explanation generation. To evaluate explanation quality, we introduce a task-specific rubric that assesses faithfulness, graph grounding, helpfulness, consistency, and conciseness, and validate it against human judgments. To focus on fine-grained details of relevant neighbors without reading the entire neighborhood, we equip a language model with graph tools that progressively disclose neighbor records. To train our graph agent, we propose a rubric-guided trajectory distillation strategy through which the agent learns both tool-use behavior and structured explanation generation. Experimental results on three fraud datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines under a human-aligned rubric.

Abstract
This work investigates the application of the Membership Inference Test (MINT) to large language models (LLMs) fine-tuned with LoRA, aiming to determine whether specific samples were used during training and address concerns about data privacy, leakage, and transparency. Building on our previous LoRA-MINT framework, which relies exclusively on perplexity under a strict black-box setting, we propose an approach based on intermediate model representations, including activations and parameter-dependent signals. These representations enable a MINT classifier to distinguish training from non-training samples without requiring full access to model parameters. We evaluated the method on four LLMs (Qwen, Phi-4, DeepSeek-V3, and LLaMA 3.2-3B) fine-tuned on three datasets covering medical, mathematical, and academic reasoning tasks. Results show consistent performance across architectures and domains, achieving scores between 95% and 98%, with robustness to variations in model configurations and data distributions. The proposed approach enables efficient auditing of sensitive training data and supports data provenance and compliance with emerging privacy and AI governance regulations. Although our experiments focus on LoRA-based fine-tuning, the methodology can be extended to other LLM adaptation techniques and, more broadly, to other AI models.
Chinese Translation
本工作研究了成员推断测试（MINT）在采用LoRA微调的大语言模型（LLM）中的应用，旨在确定特定样本是否在训练期间被使用，并应对有关数据隐私、泄漏和透明度的担忧。在我们此前仅依赖严格黑盒设置下困惑度的LoRA-MINT框架基础上，我们提出了一种基于中间模型表示的方法，包括激活值和依赖参数的信号。这些表示使MINT分类器能够区分训练样本与非训练样本，而无需完全访问模型参数。我们在四个LLM（Qwen、Phi-4、DeepSeek-V3和LLaMA 3.2-3B）上评估了该方法，这些模型在涵盖医学、数学和学术推理任务的三个数据集上进行了微调。结果表明，在不同架构和领域上性能一致，得分在95%到98%之间，并且对模型配置和数据分布的变化具有鲁棒性。所提出的方法能够高效审计敏感训练数据，并支持数据溯源以及遵守新兴的隐私和AI治理法规。尽管我们的实验聚焦于基于LoRA的微调，但该方法可以扩展到其他LLM适配技术，更广泛地说，也可以扩展到其他AI模型。

cs.LG / 96 / 2610.18108
A CaLLM Judge is a Better Judge: Mitigating Bias in LLM-as-a-judge
CaLLM 评判者是更好的评判者：缓解 LLM 充当评判者时的偏差
Cesare Barbera, Luca Stradiotti, Lorenzo Cascioli, Lorenzo Perini, Niek Tax, Daniel Haimovich, Jesse Davis, Andrea Passerini, Andrea Pugnana
cs.LG · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges to predict which of two candidate answers a human evaluator would prefer, providing a scalable alternative when human evaluation is too costly. Unfortunately, LLM judgments can exhibit systematic biases. Prior work has documented position, verbosity or model family of the candidate answers influencing the judge decision rather than their quality, while additional biases may remain undocumented. $\textit{Multicalibration}$ provides a natural framework to address this problem: each bias corresponds to miscalibration on an identifiable group, $\textit{e.g.}$, family bias manifests as overconfidence in answers generated by models belonging to the same family of the judge. The challenge is to fix miscalibration simultaneously across many, potentially unknown groups. To this end, we introduce $\mathrm{CaLLM}$, a post hoc framework that multicalibrates an LLM judge, thereby bounding all such biases simultaneously. We prove that $\mathrm{CaLLM}$ bounds the bias of every group whose error structure is captured by an available representation, and that augmenting it with explicit bias groups further reduces the residual bias. We then derive theoretical conditions under which $\mathrm{CaLLM}$ improves the judge's accuracy, rather than trading it for calibration. Finally, we evaluate $\mathrm{CaLLM}$ across pairwise preference benchmarks, showing that it reduces the multicalibration error on both specified and unspecified bias groups, while improving predictive performance of the judge.
Chinese Translation
大型语言模型（LLMs）正越来越多地被用作评判者，以预测人类评估者会偏好两个候选答案中的哪一个，在人类评估过于昂贵时提供了一种可扩展的替代方案。不幸的是，LLM 判断可能表现出系统性偏差。先前工作已经记录了候选答案的位置、冗长程度或模型家族会影响评判者决策，而非其质量，同时其他偏差可能仍未被记录。$\textit{Multicalibration}$ 为解决这个问题提供了一个自然的框架：每个偏差都对应于一个可识别群体上的误校准，$\textit{e.g.}$，家族偏差表现为对由与评判者属于同一家族的模型生成的答案的过度自信。挑战在于同时在许多可能未知的群体上修复误校准。为此，我们引入 $\mathrm{CaLLM}$，这是一个事后框架，可对 LLM 评判者进行多重校准，从而同时限制所有此类偏差。我们证明，$\mathrm{CaLLM}$ 会限制其误差结构被可用表示所捕获的每个群体的偏差，并且用显式偏差群体增强它会进一步减少残余偏差。然后，我们推导出理论条件，在这些条件下，$\mathrm{CaLLM}$ 会提高评判者的准确率，而不是以准确率换取校准。最后，我们在成对偏好基准上评估 $\mathrm{CaLLM}$，表明它在指定和未指定的偏差群体上都降低了多重校准误差，同时提高了评判者的预测性能。

A Few More Tokens Ahead: Reinforcing Parallelism in Diffusion LLMs
前方再多几个词元：强化扩散大语言模型中的并行性
Jiahao Kuang, Yangfan Gao, Tao Gui, Yuanbin Wu, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang, Tao Ji
cs.LG · cs.AI
diffusionlarge language model
扩散模型相关
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Parallel generation is widely regarded as an inherent advantage of diffusion large language models. Yet our fixed-quota evaluation of four representative models reveals severe degradation across mathematics and code, with all scores below 15% at 16 tokens per step. Token-level probes identify local predictive potential near the observed prefix, especially in mathematical text. We propose RePara, which reinforces short consecutive token blocks through group-relative policy optimization and reduces rollout and log-probability recomputation costs. On LLaDA and SDAR, \ours improves GSM8K and MATH-500 accuracy over JustGRPO under reduced denoising budgets, with a 1.96x training-step speedup in our LLaDA/MATH setup.

PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
PING：用于平流-扩散过程的物理信息图神经网络及其在太阳能功率预测中的应用
Jelena Simeunović, Baptiste Schubnel, Pierre-Jean Alet, Pascal Frossard, Rafael E. Carrillo
cs.LG · eess.SP
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Advection-diffusion plays an essential role in transport phenomena such as atmospheric and cloud dynamics. Improved forecasting of cloud motion, in turn, enhances solar power production forecasts and facilitates the integration of additional photovoltaic (PV) sources into the power grid. However, both classical numerical models and emerging deep learning approaches face challenges when applied to spatially irregular sensor networks such as those formed by weather stations. In this work, we adopt a graph signal processing perspective and model advection-diffusion particles as signals on a graph to capture the dynamics of these processes. We introduce a Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PING) for forecasting future advection-diffusion particle concentrations on irregular grids. The model incorporates a discretized advection-diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the loss function to guide learning toward physically consistent solutions. This model is on par with state of the art models on synthetic and real transport phenomena datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index datasets. Furthermore, the PING model is successfully coupled with models for forecasting PV power production. This hybrid approach leverages data fusion from ground-based sensors at PV stations and satellite images with cloud concentration to improve the accuracy of intra-day PV power production.

PRISM: Calibrating Black-Box Judges with Counterfactual Probes
PRISM：用反事实探针校准黑盒评判器
Kakei Yamamoto, So Kuroki
cs.LG · cs.AI · cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models are increasingly used as judges to reduce reliance on costly human evaluation, yet their scores can systematically disagree with human judgments. We ask whether responses to an explicitly imposed evaluative bias can help correct a judge's implicit scoring biases. We introduce PRISM (Probe-based Residual Inference of Scoring Misalignment), which holds the evaluated content fixed and measures score changes when attributes are emphasized or de-emphasized. A local sensitivity model motivates representing these responses as a surrogate Jacobian. Ridge regression on human labels learns a correction to the baseline score. The resulting scoring protocol is rubric-free: it uses overall scores without requesting criterion-level ratings. In the main Jev and Sol comparisons on SummEval summarization and HANNA story evaluation, PRISM and its learned-baseline variant significantly improve agreement with human rankings over uncalibrated scores while remaining competitive with rubric-based methods. A controlled SummEval comparison yields similar agreement for rubric-derived quality probes and style probes, supporting calibration without reproducing rubric criteria. The learned coefficients reveal shared and opposing correction directions across judges.

cs.LG / 100 / 2610.18407
Multi-Stream Residual Computation in Diffusion Language Models
扩散语言模型中的多流残差计算
Ekaterina Alimaskina, Suren Kazarian, Gleb Molodtsov, Aleksandr Beznosikov
cs.LG · cs.CL
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion language models reconstruct masked tokens in parallel, offering an alternative to autoregressive generation. Yet their Transformer backbones typically carry visible evidence and evolving masked predictions through a single residual stream. We equip masked diffusion models with multiple residual streams that persist through depth and adaptive routing between them, then investigate how they support these complementary roles. On the pretraining task, two streams reduce reconstruction perplexity by 5.71% on validation data and 5.13% on average across external corpora compared with standard residual connections. We observe that, without predefined roles, visible and masked positions learn distinct routing patterns. Causal interventions show that this distinction organizes read and write routing, while token-specific write strength remains important within each role. Guided by these findings, a model trained with role-conditioned routing recovers half the validation gain from adding a second stream. State interventions explain the benefit of the additional stream: it preserves early token representations for later reuse while evidence accumulates at masked positions. This mechanism recurs at a larger model scale, showing how persistent streams support context preservation alongside prediction refinement.

MultiAlloc: Budget-Aware Precision Allocation for KV Cache Quantization
MultiAlloc：面向 KV 缓存量化的预算感知精度分配
Yangchengyu Zhou, Zhiping Wu, Runchang Jiang, Dongdong Ren, Youfang Han, Wei Zhao, Dongqi Cai, Wenbin Li
cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
The Key-Value (KV) cache constitutes a dominant source of memory consumption during large language model (LLM) inference, particularly in long-context and complex reasoning scenarios. Existing KV cache quantization methods have explored different compression granularities, including layer-wise precision adjustment and token-level information preservation. In practical deployment, however, the key challenge is not merely compression, but how to allocate limited quantization resources among heterogeneous precision preservation strategies under a fixed KV cache memory budget. We propose MultiAlloc, a profiling-guided precision allocation framework for KV cache quantization that adaptively distributes limited quantization resources between layer-wise precision enhancement and token-wise preservation. MultiAlloc employs lightweight offline profiling to characterize layer sensitivity and token importance, enabling adaptive precision allocation under a fixed memory constraint. Guided by the profiled memory--accuracy trade-off, it automatically derives an effective precision allocation strategy without online allocation search, and applies the resulting policy during inference. Extensive experiments on reasoning and long-context benchmarks demonstrate that MultiAlloc consistently improves over layer-wise, token-wise, and recent multi-granularity KV cache quantization methods under matched memory budgets across diverse models, including Mistral, Llama, DeepSeek-Qwen, and QwQ.

键值（KV）缓存是大语言模型（LLM）推理过程中内存消耗的主要来源，在长上下文和复杂推理场景中尤为如此。现有的 KV 缓存量化方法已经探索了不同的压缩粒度，包括逐层精度调整和词元级信息保留。然而在实际部署中，关键挑战并不仅仅是压缩，而是在固定的 KV 缓存内存预算下，如何在异质的精度保留策略之间分配有限的量化资源。我们提出了 MultiAlloc，一个用于 KV 缓存量化的、由剖析引导的精度分配框架，它能够在逐层精度增强与逐词元保留之间自适应地分配有限的量化资源。MultiAlloc 采用轻量级的离线剖析来刻画层敏感性和词元重要性，从而在固定内存约束下实现自适应精度分配。在剖析得到的内存--精度权衡的引导下，它无需在线分配搜索即可自动推导出有效的精度分配策略，并在推理过程中应用所得到的策略。在推理和长上下文基准上的大量实验表明，在匹配的内存预算下，MultiAlloc 在包括 Mistral、Llama、DeepSeek-Qwen 和 QwQ 在内的多种模型上均持续优于逐层、逐词元以及近期的多粒度 KV 缓存量化方法。

cs.LG / 102 / 2610.18658
BridgeTwist: Twisting Schrödinger Bridges for Training-Free Conditional Sampling
BridgeTwist：为免训练条件采样扭转薛定谔桥
Mengyu Li, Qianqian Qu, Jun S. Liu
cs.LG · stat.ML
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Generative models are often required to serve many downstream conditional tasks. In the training-free setting, a pretrained unconditional model is reused as a prior and combined with a task-specific likelihood to sample from the corresponding posterior. While such training-free samplers have been developed for diffusion and flow models, their counterpart for Schrödinger bridge (SB) models remains unexplored, despite the growing appeal of SBs as flexible stochastic transport models between general source and target distributions. We propose BridgeTwist, a training-free conditional sampler for pretrained SB generative models, formulated as a tempered twisted sequential Monte Carlo scheme. Its twist is a closed-form plug-in surrogate, obtained by combining the velocity and score fields exposed by SB pretraining into an endpoint predictor and evaluating the likelihood there. Since this surrogate is less reliable near the source, we temper the twist with a time-varying exponent, downweighting its influence at early steps. We further introduce a bridge-shaped inference-time diffusion schedule that concentrates the proposal noise in the interior of the path. Telescoping importance weights then cancel all intermediate twist factors, yielding an asymptotically exact sampler for the posterior. Empirically, BridgeTwist outperforms training-free baselines on class-conditional and text-prompted image generation, and is competitive with specialized inverse problem solvers on inpainting, deblurring, and super-resolution.
Chinese Translation
生成模型通常需要服务于许多下游条件任务。在免训练设置中，一个预训练的无条件模型被重用为先验，并与任务特定的似然结合，以从相应后验中采样。虽然这类免训练采样器已被开发用于扩散模型和流模型，但其用于薛定谔桥（SB）模型的对应方案仍未被探索，尽管 SB 作为一般源分布和目标分布之间灵活的随机传输模型日益具有吸引力。我们提出 BridgeTwist，一种用于预训练 SB 生成模型的免训练条件采样器，其被表述为带温度调节的扭转序贯蒙特卡洛方案。其扭转项是一个闭式即插即用代理，通过将 SB 预训练所暴露的速度场和得分场组合成一个端点预测器，并在该处评估似然而获得。由于该代理在源附近不太可靠，我们用一个随时间变化的指数对扭转项进行温度调节，在早期步骤中降低其影响。我们进一步引入一种桥形推理时扩散调度，将提议噪声集中在路径的内部。随后，叠缩重要性权重抵消所有中间扭转因子，从而得到后验的渐近精确采样器。经验上，BridgeTwist 在类别条件和文本提示图像生成上优于免训练基线，并在修复、去模糊和超分辨率上与专门的逆问题求解器相比具有竞争力。

cs.LG / 103 / 2610.18677
Model-Based Online Decision Making via Generative Trajectory Planning
基于生成式轨迹规划的基于模型的在线决策
Haldun Balim, Yilun Du, Na Li
cs.LG · cs.AI · cs.RO · eess.SY
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Online decision-making faces a tension between efficient inference and long-horizon reasoning. Value-based methods rely on short-horizon bootstrapping that limits the propagation of long-term information, while trajectory optimization methods plan explicitly but must solve a high-dimensional optimization problem at every decision step. We propose Generative Trajectory Planning (GTP), a model-based framework that addresses this tension by learning a generative model as a proposal distribution over action sequences. Instead of optimizing sequences from scratch, GTP samples candidate sequences from a diffusion prior and refines them using learned dynamics, reward, and value models, enabling efficient trajectory-level reasoning. Across continuous control and long-horizon manipulation tasks, GTP matches or exceeds state-of-the-art model-free, diffusion-policy, and model-based baselines, and remains stable in regimes where strong baselines degrade. Our results suggest that generative models are best understood not as policies, but as structured proposal distributions for planning, offering a new perspective on how to integrate generative modeling with model-based decision-making.
Chinese Translation
在线决策面临着高效推理与长时程推理之间的张力。基于价值的方法依赖于短时程的自举（bootstrapping），这限制了长期信息的传播；而轨迹优化方法则进行显式规划，但必须在每一个决策步骤求解一个高维优化问题。我们提出生成式轨迹规划（Generative Trajectory Planning, GTP），这是一个基于模型的框架，它通过将生成模型学习为动作序列上的提议分布来解决这一张力。GTP 并非从头开始优化序列，而是从扩散先验中采样候选序列，并利用学得的动力学、奖励和价值模型对其进行细化，从而实现高效的轨迹级推理。在连续控制与长时程操作任务中，GTP 达到或超越了最先进的无模型、扩散策略和基于模型的基线，并在强基线出现性能退化的情形下仍保持稳定。我们的结果表明，生成模型最好不被理解为策略，而应被理解为用于规划的结构化提议分布，这为如何将生成建模与基于模型的决策相结合提供了一个新视角。

ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
ProAS：一种面向多轮智能体强化学习的进度感知优势塑造框架
Bowen Ding, Mingda Wan, Yuhan Chen, Jiyao Yuan, Qi Zhu, Futing Wang, Heyuan Deng, Fei Mi, Lifeng Shang, Tao Lin
cs.LG · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as the primary paradigm for optimizing Large Language Model (LLM) agents, yet efficient critic-free algorithms (e.g., GRPO) suffer from a fundamental uniform credit assignment dilemma that broadcasts trajectory-level advantages equally to all actions. Our analysis reveals that this uniformity inherently reinforces structurally invalid actions in preferred trajectories and ignores the downstream cascading influence of early pivotal deviations in unpreferred ones. To resolve this without introducing critic overhead, we propose Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping (ProAS), a plug-and-play framework that leverages a dynamically evolving Agentic Reference Graph (ARG) to achieve fine-grained credit assignment via Masking Unreasonable Incentives (MUI) and Asymmetric Penalty Redistribution (APR). Extensive experiments across Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct demonstrate that ProAS universally elevates mainstream group-based baselines to new state-of-the-art performance, achieving peak success rates of 91.9\% and 94.3\% on ALFWorld, alongside 66.7\% and 70.8\% on WebShop, respectively. Furthermore, it accelerates training convergence by up to $2.44\times$ while maintaining strong robustness against imperfect or distilled ARGs. Codes: https://github.com/LINs-lab/ProAS.
Chinese Translation
强化学习（RL）已成为优化大型语言模型（LLM）智能体的主要范式，然而高效的无评论家算法（例如 GRPO）受困于一个根本性的均匀信用分配困境，即将轨迹级优势均等地广播给所有动作。我们的分析表明，这种均匀性在偏好轨迹中会固有地强化结构上无效的动作，并忽略非偏好轨迹中早期关键偏差的下游级联影响。为了在不引入评论家开销的情况下解决这一问题，我们提出了进度感知优势塑造（ProAS），这是一种即插即用的框架，它利用动态演化的智能体参考图（ARG），通过掩蔽不合理激励（MUI）和非对称惩罚重分配（APR）来实现细粒度信用分配。在 Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct 和 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 上进行的大量实验表明，ProAS 普遍地将主流的基于组的基线提升到新的最先进性能，分别在 ALFWorld 上达到 91.9\% 和 94.3\% 的峰值成功率，并在 WebShop 上达到 66.7\% 和 70.8\%。此外，它最高可将训练收敛加速 $2.44\times$，同时对不完美或蒸馏得到的 ARG 保持强鲁棒性。代码：https://github.com/LINs-lab/ProAS。

SP$^2$ec: Adaptive Self-Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
SP$^2$ec：面向视觉语言模型的自适应自推测解码
Yuqi Huang, Xingyao Li, Yunlong Hou, Fengzhuo Zhang, Jiachun Pan, Vincent Y. F. Tan
cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Speculative Decoding (SD) has demonstrated its efficacy in accelerating large language model inference, but for Vision-Language Models (VLMs), the diverse input modalities make it difficult for a small trained drafter to achieve consistently high throughput. Self-speculative decoding reuses parts of the target model as a drafter which retains the multi-modal capability of the VLMs, yet its efficiency depends on choosing a suitable draft configuration for each prompt. We propose Single-Peak SPeculative decoding (SP$^2$ec), a training-free bandit algorithm that adapts the draft configuration during generation. SP$^2$ec exploits the single-peak throughput pattern observed in existing self-speculative methods, including SWIFT, KnapSpec, SpecVLM, and our simple cosSim. Our algorithmic design explicitly minimizes a novel notion of wall-time regret for each given query, corresponding to the empirical wall-time latency. Theoretical guarantees on the wall-time regret show that SP$^2$ec can exploit the optimal draft configuration, with negligible exploration cost. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B across visual and textual tasks show consistent improvements of up to 11\% over the original self-speculative methods, demonstrating the wide applicability of the proposed SP$^2$ec algorithm.
Chinese Translation
推测解码（SD）已证明其在加速大语言模型推理方面的有效性，但对于视觉语言模型（VLM）而言，多样化的输入模态使得小型训练过的草稿模型难以持续获得高吞吐量。自推测解码复用目标模型的部分作为草稿器，从而保留 VLM 的多模态能力，但其效率取决于为每个提示选择合适的草稿配置。我们提出单峰推测解码（SP$^2$ec），一种无需训练的多臂老虎机算法，在生成过程中自适应调整草稿配置。SP$^2$ec 利用了现有自推测方法中观察到的单峰吞吐量模式，这些方法包括 SWIFT、KnapSpec、SpecVLM，以及我们简单的 cosSim。我们的算法设计显式最小化针对每个给定查询的一种新颖的墙钟时间遗憾概念，该概念对应于经验墙钟时间延迟。关于墙钟时间遗憾的理论保证表明，SP$^2$ec 能够利用最优草稿配置，且探索成本可忽略不计。在 Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct 和 LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B 上跨视觉和文本任务的大量实验表明，相较于原始自推测方法，性能持续提升最高达 11\%，这证明了所提出的 SP$^2$ec 算法的广泛适用性。

SkillScaffold: Scaffolding Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Policy-Adaptive Skill Credit Assignment and Selective Injection
SkillScaffold：以策略自适应技能信用分配和选择性注入为智能体强化学习搭建脚手架
Wenlin Zhong, Hao Wang, Kun Yuan, Fan Yang, Jinluan Yang, Dian Jin, Xu Tan, Yiquan Wu, Kun Kuang
cs.LG · cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) enables large language models (LLMs) to learn from multi-turn interactions with verifiable outcomes. Textual skills can improve exploration by distilling prior interactions into reusable guidance. However, existing skill-based RL approaches often either assume skill injection is beneficial or rely on indirect feedback or rollout-intensive evaluation to assess its utility. Our pilot studies show that rollout-based utility estimation for skill credit assignment is costly and unstable under limited sampling, while skill benefits vary across candidates and depend on the current policy's competence on each query. To address these challenges, we introduce SkillScaffold, a policy-adaptive training scaffold that combines low-cost skill-utility estimation with selective skill injection. By reusing outcome-verified training trajectories, SkillScaffold generates candidate skills and estimates their utility through outcome-aware likelihood comparisons, without candidate-specific environment rollouts. The resulting utility guides whether and which skill to inject, retaining skill-free execution when no candidate is estimated to help. Joint training enables the Generator to produce skills tailored to the evolving Executor. Scaffolded RL encourages skill internalization for skill-free inference. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld, and $τ^2$-Bench demonstrate gains over strong agentic-RL and skill-based RL baselines across both short- and long-horizon tasks. Ablations and further analyses support the importance of utility-based selection and abstention. Our code is available at https://github.com/Vaidurya00/SkillScaffold.
Chinese Translation
智能体强化学习（RL）使大语言模型（LLMs）能够从具有可验证结果的多轮交互中学习。文本技能可以通过将先前交互蒸馏为可复用的指导来改善探索。然而，现有的基于技能的 RL 方法通常要么假设技能注入是有益的，要么依赖间接反馈或 rollout 密集型的评估来评估其效用。我们的初步研究表明，用于技能信用分配的基于 rollout 的效用估计成本高昂，且在有限采样下不稳定；同时，技能收益在不同候选技能之间存在差异，并取决于当前策略在每个查询上的能力。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 SkillScaffold，一种策略自适应的训练脚手架，它将低成本的技能效用估计与选择性技能注入相结合。通过复用经结果验证的训练轨迹，SkillScaffold 生成候选技能，并通过结果感知的似然比较来估计其效用，而无需特定于候选技能的环境 rollout。所得效用指导是否注入技能以及注入哪个技能；当估计没有任何候选技能有帮助时，则保留无技能执行。联合训练使 Generator 能够生成针对不断演化的 Executor 量身定制的技能。脚手架式 RL 鼓励技能内化，以实现无技能推理。在 ALFWorld、WebShop、ScienceWorld 和 $τ^2$-Bench 上的实验表明，在短时程和长时程任务上，相较于强智能体 RL 和基于技能的 RL 基线均取得了提升。消融实验和进一步分析支持了基于效用的选择与弃权的重要性。我们的代码可在 https://github.com/Vaidurya00/SkillScaffold 获取。

cs.MA / 107 / 2610.17751
Degrees of Freedom in Multi-Agent Coordination: Between Centralized and Decentralized Regimes
多智能体协调中的自由度：在集中式与分散式机制之间
Yiqing Peng, Hehai Lin, Zixuan Wang, Dongyi Zhang, Zhengjie Zhu, Yi Han, Yangyang Zheng, Hao Wang, Qian Li, Chengwei Qin
cs.MA · cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) are commonly organized around two coordination regimes. Centralized coordination provides explicit control but can create a bottleneck at a single coordination locus, whereas decentralized coordination offers local autonomy but must achieve effective collaboration through distributed decisions and experience. These trade-offs motivate a systematic study of the space between the two regimes. We introduce Degrees of Freedom (DoF), a continuous configuration framework that quantifies the size of the decision space delegated to downstream agents. DoF controls the granularity of delegated work and the target probability that each task unit is assigned to the branches. Its endpoints recover the two coordination regimes. Across multiple task domains, DoF reveals a hierarchy of organizational effects. Delegated granularity and within-regime routing produce structured but bounded profile reallocations, whereas task domain and retained experience are associated with stronger differences between the centralized- and decentralized-branch profiles. The resulting performance landscape is task-dependent: different domains favor different DoF configurations, while atomic-target conditions are more consistent across runs. In-domain retained experience brings the two branch profiles closer together. The same controlled sweep reveals a task-dependent coordination landscape: some domains exhibit higher-performing configurations, whereas others show flatter responses and no single configuration dominates across domains. In five of the six evaluated state, an intermediate DoF configuration achieves higher mean accuracy than both endpoints, demonstrating the value of exploring the coordination space between them. Together, these findings provide empirical guidance for studying and designing intermediate coordination regimes in LLM-based MAS.
Chinese Translation
基于大语言模型（LLM）的多智能体系统（MAS）通常围绕两种协调机制进行组织。集中式协调提供了显式控制，但可能在单一协调节点处造成瓶颈；而分散式协调提供了局部自主性，但必须通过分布式决策与经验来实现有效协作。这些权衡促使我们对两种机制之间的空间进行系统性研究。我们引入自由度（DoF），一个连续的配置框架，用于量化委派给下游智能体的决策空间的大小。DoF 控制所委派工作的粒度以及每个任务单元被分配到各分支的目标概率。其两个端点分别还原了这两种协调机制。在多个任务领域中，DoF 揭示了一种组织效应的层级结构。委派粒度与机制内路由产生了结构化但有界的配置重分配，而任务领域与保留经验则与集中式分支配置和分散式分支配置之间更强的差异相关。由此产生的性能景观依赖于任务：不同领域偏好不同的 DoF 配置，而原子目标条件在不同运行之间更为一致。领域内保留经验使两种分支配置更加接近。同一受控扫描揭示了一种依赖于任务的协调景观：一些领域表现出性能更高的配置，而另一些领域则呈现更平坦的响应，并且没有任何单一配置在所有领域中都占主导。在六个被评估状态中的五个里，一种中间 DoF 配置取得了高于两个端点的平均准确率，这表明了探索二者之间协调空间的价值。总体而言，这些发现为研究和设计基于 LLM 的 MAS 中的中间协调机制提供了实证指导。

How Reliable Are Large Language Models for Soil Organic Carbon Assessment? An Australian Benchmark
大型语言模型在土壤有机碳评估中有多可靠？一项澳大利亚基准测试
Yingxuan Cheng, Tong Li, Yayong Li, Yuchuan Fan, You-Gan Wang, Jinran Wu, Scott Chapman, Geoffrey J. McLachlan
cs.PF · cs.AI · cs.CY
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Soil organic carbon (SOC) is an indicator of agricultural soil condition and carbon storage, but numerical outputs from large language models (LLMs) require validation before use in monitoring or management. We evaluated seven general-purpose LLM configurations on three direct-response tasks: estimating 0--10 cm SOC concentrations for 308 Australian paddocks under two information conditions, calculating SOC stock in 120 matched scenarios, and comparing 300 paddock pairs. References were measured SOC records or deterministic calculations; response validity, repeated-call dispersion and estimated API cost were assessed separately. Additional measured soil attributes reduced concentration mean absolute error by 13--62\% across configurations, although high-SOC underprediction and paddock-specific errors persisted. Six configurations were highly accurate in stock calculations using equation-native units without coarse fragments, but accuracy declined with physically equivalent alternative units. Pairwise accuracy was 90.5--94.6\% overall and 59.1--70.9\% for 52 closely separated pairs; some configurations were sensitive to presentation order. Nearly all outputs were parseable, without necessarily being correct. The benchmark identifies three distinct requirements for AI-mediated SOC assessment: agreement with measured concentrations, unit-consistent stock calculations and reliable discrimination between sites. These findings support task-specific validation and auditable calculations, rather than unverified use of LLM outputs as ecological evidence.
Chinese Translation
土壤有机碳（SOC）是农业土壤状况和碳储量的一个指标，但来自大型语言模型（LLM）的数值输出在用于监测或管理之前需要验证。我们在三项直接响应任务上评估了七种通用 LLM 配置：在两种信息条件下估算 308 个澳大利亚围场 0--10 cm 的 SOC 浓度，在 120 个匹配情景中计算 SOC 储量，以及比较 300 对围场。参考值为实测 SOC 记录或确定性计算；响应有效性、重复调用离散度和估计的 API 成本分别进行了评估。额外的实测土壤属性使不同配置下的浓度平均绝对误差降低了 13--62\%，尽管高 SOC 低估和特定围场误差仍然存在。六种配置在使用不含粗碎屑的方程原生单位进行储量计算时高度准确，但使用物理等价的替代单位时准确率下降。成对准确率总体上为 90.5--94.6\%，而对于 52 对差异很小的配对为 59.1--70.9\%；一些配置对呈现顺序敏感。几乎所有输出都可解析，但不一定正确。该基准确定了 AI 介导的 SOC 评估的三项不同要求：与实测浓度一致、单位一致的储量计算，以及可靠区分不同地点。这些发现支持针对特定任务的验证和可审计计算，而不是将 LLM 输出未经核实地用作生态证据。

PrT-Flow: Probability-Tractable Flow Matching for Reinforcement Learning
PrT-Flow：面向强化学习的概率可处理流匹配
Congzhong Sun, Ning Tan
cs.RO · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion models and Flow Matching can represent flexible distributions over robot actions, but many reinforcement learning algorithms also require the probability of each action. We introduce PrT-Flow (Probability-Tractable Flow Matching), which computes probability density while retaining multimodal, multi-step action generation. Its Jacobian-Tractable Transformer (JTT) makes each sampling step invertible and enables efficient computation of its Jacobian determinant. We train these finite steps with Conditional Euler-step Training (CET), which supervises their displacement over one step during sampling rather than their instantaneous velocity. We prove that, under certain assumptions, CET has the same minimizers as fitting the Euler-solver updates of Flow Matching. PrT-Flow achieves 96% success on Robomimic Lift after 300 epochs of imitation learning, matching the diffusion policy reference, and 96% success on OGBench Cube-Triple after 600k online steps. These results demonstrate that invertible networks with tractable probability densities can learn effective robot policies and support SAC-style actor-critic training. Our code is available at https://github.com/Sunlight-zero/PrT-Flow .

扩散模型和流匹配可以表示机器人动作上的灵活分布，但许多强化学习算法还需要每个动作的概率。我们提出 PrT-Flow（Probability-Tractable Flow Matching，概率可处理的流匹配），它在保留多模态、多步动作生成的同时计算概率密度。其雅可比可处理 Transformer（Jacobian-Tractable Transformer，JTT）使每个采样步骤可逆，并能够高效计算其雅可比行列式。我们使用条件欧拉步训练（Conditional Euler-step Training，CET）来训练这些有限步骤，它监督采样过程中一步上的位移，而不是其瞬时速度。我们证明，在一定假设下，CET 与拟合流匹配的欧拉求解器更新具有相同的最小值点。PrT-Flow 在 300 个轮次的模仿学习后在 Robomimic Lift 上达到 96% 的成功率，与扩散策略参考持平，并在 600k 在线步骤后在 OGBench Cube-Triple 上达到 96% 的成功率。这些结果表明，具有可处理概率密度的可逆网络可以学习有效的机器人策略，并支持 SAC 风格的 actor-critic 训练。我们的代码可在 https://github.com/Sunlight-zero/PrT-Flow 获取。

UniW(A)M: A Unified Mixture-of-Experts Framework for World and World-Action Models

Jingbo Xu, Jianjie Fang, Zhuohang Li, Zihao Song, Zhaolu Wang, Xvyuan Liu, Xin Zhang, Haisheng Su, Yinzhou Tang, Chen Gao, Wei Wu, Yong Li
cs.RO · cs.AI · cs.CV · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
World models (WMs) and world-action models (WAMs) focus on future world prediction and executable action generation, respectively. Although these models learn shared physical dynamics and interaction semantics from embodied trajectories, they are typically trained in isolation, which restricts knowledge reuse between prediction and control. The central challenge is therefore to develop a unified learning framework that shares these dynamics while preserving the distinct modeling capabilities required by each paradigm. We propose UniW(A)M, a mixture-of-experts world-(action) model built upon diffusion Transformers that unifies action-conditioned world modeling and diverse WAM variants. Shared experts capture common dynamics, while atomic capability experts are reused across interfaces so that each interface keeps its own conditional pathway. At deployment, a plug-in adaptive interface router (PAIR) learns from a small subset of target-task chunk scenarios to select a suitable WAM interface for each execution chunk, balancing task success and execution efficiency while keeping the backbone frozen. We evaluate UniW(A)M on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and three real-world manipulation tasks, where it achieves 88.3% average real-world success versus 76.7% for the strongest baseline. On WorldArena, it leads action-conditioned world modeling on all three tasks. AC-WM co-training contributes to action generation on every action interface and PAIR raises OOD success from 63.3% to 76.7%.

世界模型（WMs）与世界-动作模型（WAMs）分别关注未来世界预测与可执行动作生成。尽管这些模型从具身轨迹中学习共享的物理动力学与交互语义，但它们通常被孤立地训练，这限制了预测与控制之间的知识复用。因此，核心挑战在于开发一个统一的学习框架，在共享这些动力学的同时，保留每种范式各自所需的独特建模能力。我们提出 UniW(A)M，一个基于扩散 Transformer 构建的专家混合世界-（动作）模型，它统一了动作条件世界建模与多样化的 WAM 变体。共享专家捕获共同的动力学，而原子能力专家在各接口之间被复用，使得每个接口保留自身的条件路径。在部署时，一个即插即用的自适应接口路由器（PAIR）从目标任务片段场景的一小部分子集中学习，为每个执行片段选择合适的 WAM 接口，在保持骨干网络冻结的同时平衡任务成功率与执行效率。我们在 LIBERO、RoboTwin 2.0 以及三个真实世界操作任务上评估 UniW(A)M，其平均真实世界成功率达到 88.3%，而最强基线为 76.7%。在 WorldArena 上，它在全部三个任务上均领先于动作条件世界建模。AC-WM 协同训练对每个动作接口上的动作生成均有贡献，PAIR 将 OOD 成功率从 63.3% 提升至 76.7%。

cs.AI / 111 / 2610.18711
Steertuning Policies from a Few Human Videos
从少量人类视频中得到的 Steertuning 策略
Billy Yan, Isaac Tu, Kelly Lee, Blake Chang, Kenny Ma, Kanad Patel, Dhawal Kabra, Neer Patel, Kevin Wu, Lerrel Pinto, Irmak Guzey
cs.RO · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Current recipes for robot learning require massive amounts of robot demonstrations to obtain robust and adaptive policies. In this work, we introduce Steertuning, a system that enables robots to learn new tasks in new environments from 5 human demonstrations in under 5 Steertuning consists of two parts. (1) We pretrain a 400M-parameter diffusion policy on our egocentric human dataset, which consists of 100 hours of densely annotated random interactions. This pretraining makes Steertuning robust to background differences and enables spatial and object generalization when deployed on new tasks. (2) Given 5 demonstrations of a new task, we finetune our model for only 2 minutes (2000 training updates) and steer the policy's actions during reverse sampling using the demonstration whose observation is closest to that of the deployment environment. Together with a carefully designed data processing pipeline for embodiment transfer, this enables Steertuning to achieve a 71% success rate across 12 tasks in 12 new environments, ranging from lab settings to kitchens in new homes. The entire process, from data collection for a new task to robot policy deployment, takes less than 5 minutes. Our full dataset, model weights, codebase, and robot videos will be made available at our website: https://steertuning.github.io.
Chinese Translation
当前机器人学习的方案需要大量机器人演示，以获得鲁棒且自适应的策略。在这项工作中，我们提出了 Steertuning，一个使机器人能够从 5 个人类演示中在不到 5 分钟内学习新环境中的新任务的系统。Steertuning 由两部分组成。（1）我们在以自我为中心的人类数据集上预训练一个 400M 参数的扩散策略，该数据集由 100 小时密集标注的随机交互组成。这种预训练使 Steertuning 对背景差异具有鲁棒性，并在部署到新任务时实现空间和物体泛化。（2）给定一个新任务的 5 个演示，我们仅用 2 分钟（2000 次训练更新）微调我们的模型，并在反向采样期间使用其观测与部署环境的观测最接近的演示来引导策略的动作。结合一个为具身迁移精心设计的数据处理流水线，这使 Steertuning 在 12 个新环境中的 12 个任务上实现了 71% 的成功率，这些环境从实验室环境到新住宅中的厨房不等。整个过程，从新任务的数据收集到机器人策略部署，耗时不到 5 分钟。我们的完整数据集、模型权重、代码库和机器人视频将在我们的网站提供：https://steertuning.github.io。

cs.AI / 112 / 2610.18874
ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
ChunkAct：面向智能体机器人的动作分块
Bingxin Xu, Wenrui Bao, Xinxin Liu, Jiawei Zhou, Yuzhang Shang, Emilio Ferrara
cs.RO · cs.AI · cs.CL · cs.CV
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Agentic robotics places a large language model (LLM) agent in the robot control loop, where it composes perception, motion, and vision-language-action (VLA) tools under the guidance of a memory and thereby generalizes to new tasks without retraining. This generality comes at a steep price in efficiency. Every primitive requires a round of LLM reasoning over the full interaction history, so the cost of an episode grows with the number of primitives. We find this reasoning largely redundant: once a sub-goal is chosen, its primitives follow a routine already prescribed by memory. We present ChunkAct, which introduces action chunking to agentic robotics. Online, a single call launches a chunk of chained primitives, which executes autonomously and returns control only upon failure. Offline, ChunkAct compiles the memory into these chunks, so execution is memory-free at test time and the planner is reserved for decisions that require reasoning. LLM computation therefore scales with the number of decisions rather than the number of primitives. On LIBERO-Pro, ChunkAct improves task success by 5.0 points over the state of the art in agentic robotics while requiring 2.9x fewer LLM calls, 4.4x fewer input tokens, and 2.3x fewer output tokens.
Chinese Translation
智能体机器人（agentic robotics）将大语言模型（LLM）智能体置于机器人控制回路中，使其在记忆的引导下组合感知、运动与视觉-语言-动作（VLA）工具，从而无需重新训练即可泛化到新任务。这种通用性在效率上付出了高昂的代价。每个基元都需要基于完整交互历史进行一轮 LLM 推理，因此一个回合的成本随基元数量的增加而增长。我们发现这种推理在很大程度上是冗余的：一旦选定某个子目标，其基元便遵循记忆已经规定的例行流程。我们提出 ChunkAct，将动作分块（action chunking）引入智能体机器人。在线时，单次调用即可启动一个由链式基元构成的分块，该分块自主执行，仅在失败时才交还控制权。离线时，ChunkAct 将记忆编译为这些分块，因此在测试时执行无需记忆，规划器仅被保留用于需要推理的决策。因此，LLM 的计算量随决策数量而非基元数量扩展。在 LIBERO-Pro 上，ChunkAct 相比智能体机器人领域的最先进方法将任务成功率提升 5.0 个百分点，同时所需 LLM 调用次数减少 2.9 倍，输入 token 减少 4.4 倍，输出 token 减少 2.3 倍。

Why Agentic Workflows Fail: A Taxonomy Derived from Literature and Empirical Data
智能体工作流为何失败：一个源自文献与实证数据的分类体系
Xin Li, Rami Bahsoon, Tao Chen
cs.SE · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Agentic workflows combine large language models with planning, memory, tools, execution environments, and iterative feedback. Their failures are difficult to diagnose because the same user-visible symptom may originate from model behavior, workflow orchestration, external tools, infrastructure, or their interaction. This paper presents a source-aware taxonomy of agentic workflow failures and applies it to evidence from academic literature and GitHub. The taxonomy combines source attribution with three empirical dimensions: a concrete failure-type dictionary, workflow-stage localization, and agent-capability localization. Its central structure is a two-axis localization matrix: workflow stages form the horizontal process axis and agent capabilities form the vertical functional axis. This design moves beyond taxonomies that mainly classify final failure manifestations by localizing intermediate process states inside agent operation. Our empirical comparison shows that literature-derived failures emphasize planning, reasoning, learning, perception, and knowledge-related mechanisms, whereas GitHub-derived failures concentrate on execution-stage, actuation-related, tool, API, and infrastructure failures. The dominant hotspot is iterative execution and actuation. These findings indicate that agentic workflow reliability should be treated as a systems problem rather than only a model-output problem. The taxonomy provides a basis for structured evaluation, root cause analysis, failure injection, and engineering triage.

Diff Diffusion: Predicting Edit Paths with Diffusion Models for Efficient Code Editing
Diff Diffusion：利用扩散模型预测编辑路径以实现高效代码编辑
Xiaolong Xu, Hao Jiang, Bo Jiang, Zhiwen Deng, Ningyuan Sun, Bingzhou Chen, Jin Chen, Chenxing Wei
cs.SE · cs.AI · cs.CL
diffusionlarge language model
扩散模型相关
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) are appealing for code generation because they can update many tokens in parallel, yet many are optimized for sequence synthesis rather than edit prediction. This setting is poorly matched to modern AI-assisted IDEs, where edit prediction must infer the next code change from recent edits, the current file, and cursor-local context. Such changes are usually sparse and preserve most source tokens, so regenerating a full code segment wastes computation. We propose Diff Diffusion, a diffusion-inspired LLM framework for code editing that predicts edit paths from an original snippet to its revised form. Diff Diffusion represents denoising as structured edit operations, and combines this formulation with multi-stage training and efficient parallel decoding. By focusing computation on changed regions, Diff Diffusion supports accurate low-latency edits and multi-position parallel modification. Across public edit-completion benchmarks, edit-prediction evaluations, and online validation, Diff Diffusion matches or leads autoregressive baselines while delivering 2.78 times faster inference on public edit-completion benchmarks and a 39.0% P50 model-latency reduction in production. This work provides a new modeling perspective for AI applications that require high accuracy and low latency.
Chinese Translation
扩散大语言模型（dLLMs）在代码生成方面颇具吸引力，因为它们可以并行更新许多 token，然而其中许多模型是为序列合成而非编辑预测而优化的。这一设定与现代 AI 辅助 IDE 匹配不佳，因为在这些 IDE 中，编辑预测必须从最近的编辑、当前文件以及光标局部上下文中推断下一次代码更改。此类更改通常是稀疏的，并保留大多数源代码 token，因此重新生成完整代码段会浪费计算。我们提出 Diff Diffusion，一个受扩散启发的 LLM 代码编辑框架，它预测从原始代码片段到其修订形式的编辑路径。Diff Diffusion 将去噪表示为结构化编辑操作，并将这种表述与多阶段训练和高效并行解码相结合。通过将计算集中在更改区域，Diff Diffusion 支持准确的低延迟编辑和多位置并行修改。在公开的编辑补全基准、编辑预测评估和在线验证中，Diff Diffusion 匹配或领先于自回归基线，同时在公开编辑补全基准上实现快 2.78 倍的推理，并在生产中实现 39.0% 的 P50 模型延迟降低。这项工作为需要高精度和低延迟的 AI 应用提供了新的建模视角。

Mobile App Analysis in the New Era: Challenges and the Road Ahead
新时代的移动应用分析：挑战与前路
Jiale Wu, Tianming Liu, Yanjie Zhao, Haoyu Wang
cs.SE
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Mobile applications (apps) have grown into complex, multi-platform systems that support diverse services and operate within varying regulatory and distribution contexts. Traditional analysis techniques have established a strong foundation for ensuring quality, security, and compliance, but face increasing challenges as mobile apps evolve. This article presents a three-layer perspective to examine these challenges. The Artifact Layer highlights how heterogeneous code bases and protection mechanisms reduce the analyzability of packaged apps. The Runtime Layer addresses growing execution complexity, from multi-modal interactions and super-app architectures to AI-driven autonomous operations. The Ecosystem Layer considers broader contexts, including emerging platforms, fragmented distribution channels, and region-specific regulatory requirements. New characteristics across these layers interact and compound, creating difficulties that existing approaches are not designed to handle. For each layer, we identify key challenges and potential research directions, including framework-aware analysis, adaptive testing, and policy-aware compliance verification. We also discuss how large language models bring new analytical capabilities to the field, while their integration into apps raises new security and privacy concerns. This article aims to clarify where established methods fall short and highlight directions for future research in this evolving field.
Chinese Translation
移动应用（apps）已发展为复杂的、多平台系统，支持多样化的服务，并在各异的监管与分发环境中运行。传统分析技术为确保质量、安全与合规奠定了坚实基础，但随着移动应用的演进，它们正面临日益增多的挑战。本文提出一个三层视角来审视这些挑战。制品层（The Artifact Layer）关注异构代码库与保护机制如何降低已打包应用的可分析性。运行时层（The Runtime Layer）应对日益增长的执行复杂性，从多模态交互与超级应用架构，到由 AI 驱动的自主运行。生态层（The Ecosystem Layer）考虑更广泛的背景，包括新兴平台、碎片化的分发渠道以及特定区域的监管要求。这些层面上出现的新特性相互作用并叠加，造成现有方法在设计上无法应对的困难。针对每一层，我们识别关键挑战与潜在研究方向，包括框架感知分析、自适应测试以及策略感知的合规性验证。我们还讨论大语言模型如何为该领域带来新的分析能力，同时其集成到应用中又引发了新的安全与隐私担忧。本文旨在阐明既有方法的不足之处，并指出这一不断演进领域中未来的研究方向。

SpecCloak: Probing Harmful Code Generation through Engineering Specifications
SpecCloak：通过工程规格探查有害代码生成
Wenbin Chen, Jiexin Wang, Guanting Wu, Jiaxi Liang, Yi Cai
cs.SE · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
The code generation capabilities of large language models (LLMs) can equally be misused to implement harmful functionality, underscoring the need to understand their safety behavior in response to programming requests. While request phrasing is known to influence refusal, it remains unclear whether the form in which coding task requirements are stated affects the refusal process for malicious code generation. We introduce PseudoSpec, a template that organizes functional requirements as engineering specifications, and investigate its effects through controlled comparisons, representation analysis, and activation interventions. Across five open-weight models, removing explicit risk keywords only partially reduces refusal, whereas specification prompting substantially lowers refusal even when these keywords are retained. This reduction accompanies consistent shifts toward code-output-related representations, and interventions along condition-difference directions alter refusal behavior. Output analysis further distinguishes code-related responses from generation degeneration. Building on these findings, we propose SpecCloak, a black-box red-teaming framework combining PseudoSpec with discriminator-guided optimization, achieving an average execution-verified attack success rate of 28.91\% across eight target models on RedCode-Gen. We also introduce SpecReveal, a defense prototype combining natural-language intent reconstruction with dual-view detection without target-model fine-tuning. It achieves a 96.88\% attack detection rate in a separate prompt-detection evaluation, with false positives assessed on benign programming and specification-style inputs. These results connect specification-induced response differences to practical security consequences and identify intent reconstruction as a complementary detection approach.
Chinese Translation
大语言模型（LLMs）的代码生成能力同样可能被滥用于实现有害功能，这凸显了理解其在响应编程请求时的安全行为的必要性。尽管已知请求的措辞会影响拒绝行为，但编码任务需求的陈述形式是否会影响恶意代码生成的拒绝过程，目前仍不清楚。我们提出 PseudoSpec，一种将功能需求组织为工程规格的模板，并通过受控对比、表征分析和激活干预来研究其影响。在五个开放权重模型上，移除显式风险关键词仅能部分降低拒绝率，而即使保留这些关键词，规格化提示也能大幅降低拒绝率。这种降低伴随着向代码输出相关表征的一致偏移，而沿条件差异方向的干预会改变拒绝行为。输出分析进一步将代码相关响应与生成退化区分开来。基于这些发现，我们提出 SpecCloak，一个结合 PseudoSpec 与判别器引导优化的黑盒红队框架，在 RedCode-Gen 上于八个目标模型上实现了平均 28.91\% 的经执行验证的攻击成功率。我们还提出 SpecReveal，一个结合自然语言意图重建与双视角检测的防御原型，无需对目标模型进行微调。在单独的提示检测评估中，它实现了 96.88\% 的攻击检测率，并在良性编程与规格风格输入上评估了误报。这些结果将规格诱导的响应差异与实际安全后果联系起来，并将意图重建确定为一种互补的检测方法。

DTScribe: Generating Models for Digital Twin Reporting using Local Large Language Models
DTScribe：使用本地大型语言模型为数字孪生报告生成模型
Kérian Fiter, Angelica Portocarrero, Bentley Oakes
cs.SE · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
The development of a digital twin brings together many stakeholders and technical components. We have previously investigated the reporting of the conceptual architecture for these digital twins as an artifact for discussion. However, we find that the activity of modeling the digital twin for visualization and consensus-building can be quite tedious and time-consuming. In this article, we explore the automation of model generation using large language models, targeting the model required for digital twin reporting. Our approach is designed to ingest digital twin documents and output both the conceptual architecture visualization and a reporting page for that digital twin. We first extract from the input the key details aligning with our twenty-one-characteristic Digital Twin Description Framework described in previous work. Then, we generate a description model in the Ontological Modeling Language, representing the digital twin as a constellation of models, data, enablers, and services. We utilize refinement loops with large language models acting as judges and ontological reasoning to increase artifact quality as measured by our metrics. We investigate how architectural and parameter choices affect artifact quality, such as how refinement loops enable local large language models to produce sufficiently high-quality results comparable to larger models. We also detail insights and lessons learned useful for practitioners, such that they can integrate our techniques to accelerate their digital twin reporting or for other model generation tasks. These insights include the use of medium-sized local models (around 20 billion parameters), the avoidance of large language models as judges and clustering for characteristic extraction, and the recommendation of at least two reasoner loops for Ontological Modeling Language refinement.

SolBehave: Evaluating the Behavioural Correctness of LLM-Generated Smart Contracts
SolBehave：评估大语言模型生成的智能合约的行为正确性
Giovanni Pio Delvecchio, Stefano Fantazzini, Giacomo Frisoni, Gianluca Moro, Lorenzo Bacchiani, Mario Bravetti, Thomas Troels Hildebrandt
cs.SE · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models increasingly generate Solidity smart contracts that, once deployed, can never be patched, making a single latent fault permanent and exploitable. Yet current evaluations mostly ask only whether generated code compiles. We introduce SolBehave, a benchmark for evaluating the correctness of model-generated contracts at scale, moving beyond ad hoc unit tests. Across 250 real, reproducible Ethereum contracts, we apply three complementary tests of behavioural fidelity: differential fuzzing, historical-transaction replay, and, as our core contribution, synthetic-transaction replay guided by a Dynamic Condition Response (DCR) graph that enumerates the space of legitimate function-call sequences. Differential fuzzing compares each generated function with the original on automatically generated inputs; historical replay compares the whole contract on the transactions it actually received on-chain; DCR-guided replay compares it on sequences of calls that follow its intended usage, including orderings that never occurred on-chain. We evaluate seven state-of-the-art open-weight models after one round of automated repair. Compilation success ranges from 26.4% to 92.7%, but under differential fuzzing only 31.4% of all generated function bodies that compile, pooled over models and samples, are equivalent to the original. Divergence at the contract level is the norm rather than the exception: for six of the seven models, between 13% and 31% of the generated contracts that compile diverge from the original under historical replay, and between 13% and 44% under DCR-guided replay; only Gemma-4-31B stays below 3% on both. Compilation is therefore a necessary condition for correctness and far from a sufficient one.

大语言模型越来越多地生成 Solidity 智能合约，而这些合约一旦部署就永远无法修补，使得单个潜在故障变得永久化并可被利用。然而，当前的评估大多只关注生成的代码能否编译。我们提出 SolBehave，一个用于大规模评估模型生成合约正确性的基准，超越了临时性的单元测试。在 250 个真实、可复现的以太坊合约上，我们应用三种互补的行为保真度测试：差分模糊测试、历史交易重放，以及作为我们核心贡献的、由动态条件响应（DCR）图引导的合成交易重放，该图枚举了合法函数调用序列的空间。差分模糊测试在自动生成的输入上将每个生成的函数与原始函数进行比较；历史重放在整个合约实际在链上收到的交易上对其进行比较；DCR 引导的重放则在遵循其预期用途的调用序列上对其进行比较，包括从未在链上出现过的顺序。我们在一轮自动修复之后评估了七个最先进的开放权重模型。编译成功率介于 26.4% 到 92.7% 之间，但在差分模糊测试下，将所有模型和样本汇总计算，所有能够编译的生成函数体中只有 31.4% 与原始函数体等价。合约层面的分歧是常态而非例外：对于七个模型中的六个，其能够编译的生成合约中有 13% 到 31% 在历史重放下与原始合约产生分歧，而在 DCR 引导的重放下这一比例为 13% 到 44%；只有 Gemma-4-31B 在两项测试中均保持在 3% 以下。因此，编译通过是正确性的一个必要条件，而远非充分条件。

cs.LG / 119 / 2610.17282
Colored Graph Signal Diffusion Models
有色图信号扩散模型
Yiğit Berkay Uslu, Samar Hadou, Shirin Saeedi Bidokhti, Alejandro Ribeiro
eess.SP · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Standard diffusion processes with isotropic noise corruption are not spectrally neutral. They inherit a coarse-to-fine generation hierarchy from the nonuniform data spectrum, because each frequency band loses signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at its own rate. For signals on a graph, the relevant spectrum is that of the graph shift operator (GSO). A natural construction, therefore, builds both the diffusion dynamics and the denoiser from graph filters of the GSO, and any such design also takes a position on this hierarchy. We expose this hierarchy as a tunable axis through a family of colored score-based diffusions. Fixing the terminal prior to a Gaussian colored by the GSO couples the drift and diffusion through a positive spectral rate, which acts as a clock for each graph-frequency band. The clock sets when a band loses and recovers information, and the forward processes of standard and certain graph-aware diffusions appear as members of this family. A GSO-valued EDM preconditioning splits the denoiser into an analytic Wiener head that carries the Gaussian second-order structure and a graph neural network (GNN) that learns the remaining non-Gaussian dependencies. Numerical experiments show that colored diffusions reach a given generation quality in far fewer sampling steps than standard diffusion.

带有各向同性噪声腐蚀的标准扩散过程在频谱上并非中性。它们从非均匀的数据频谱中继承了一种从粗到细的生成层级结构，因为每个频带都以其自身的速率损失信噪比（SNR）。对于图上的信号，相关频谱是图移位算子（GSO）的频谱。因此，一种自然的构造从 GSO 的图滤波器出发来构建扩散动力学和去噪器，而任何此类设计也都在这一层级结构上占有一个位置。我们通过一族有色的基于分数的扩散，将这一层级结构揭示为一个可调轴。将终端先验固定为由 GSO 着色的高斯分布，会通过一个正谱速率把漂移与扩散耦合起来，该速率对每个图频带而言充当一个时钟。这个时钟决定了某个频带何时丢失和恢复信息，而标准扩散以及某些图感知扩散的前向过程都表现为这一族的成员。一种取值为 GSO 的 EDM 预条件将去噪器拆分为一个解析的维纳头，其承载高斯的二阶结构，以及一个图神经网络（GNN），其学习剩余的非高斯依赖关系。数值实验表明，与标准扩散相比，有色扩散能以少得多的采样步数达到给定的生成质量。

cs.LG / 120 / 2610.18863
Data Free Training of Diffusion Models for Lattice Field Theories
面向格点场论的扩散模型无数据训练
Dennis Grinwald, Ankur Singha, Khaled Kahouli, Karl Jansen, Shinichi Nakajima
hep-lat · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Sampling equilibrium field configurations remains a major computational bottleneck in lattice field theory, motivating the development of generative samplers that can produce independent configurations. Diffusion models are promising for this purpose, but their standard denoising score matching objective requires samples from the target distribution, seemingly reintroducing the original sampling problem. Here, we show that diffusion models can instead be trained from their own generated samples using the target score identity, provided access to the unnormalized probability density. Importance-weighted formulations of this identity yield a consistent target throughout training, while unweighted variants define a self-consistent fixed-point training scheme. We benchmark the different approaches in two-dimensional \(φ^4\) theory and identify effective choices that enable efficient training and sampling across the symmetric, critical, and broken phases. Ultimately, our data-free training approach achieves comparable performance to training on HMC reference data.
Chinese Translation
对平衡场构型进行采样仍然是格点场论中的一个主要计算瓶颈，这推动了能够产生独立构型的生成式采样器的发展。扩散模型对此很有前景，但其标准的去噪分数匹配目标需要来自目标分布的样本，这似乎重新引入了原本的采样问题。在这里，我们表明，只要能够获得未归一化的概率密度，扩散模型反而可以利用目标分数恒等式从其自身生成的样本中进行训练。该恒等式的重要性加权形式在整个训练过程中产生一致的目标，而未加权变体则定义了一种自洽的不动点训练方案。我们在二维 \(φ^4\) 理论中对这些不同方法进行了基准测试，并确定了能够在对称相、临界相和破缺相中实现高效训练和采样的有效选择。最终，我们的无数据训练方法取得了与在 HMC 参考数据上训练相当的性能。

How Well Do LLMs Perform in Peer Review? Evidence from Finance and Accounting
大语言模型在同行评审中表现如何？来自金融与会计领域的证据
Hai Lu, Yichen Luo, Luping Yu
q-fin.GN · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Referees increasingly use large language models (LLMs), while finance and accounting journals disagree about whether to allow it. We ask which part of a referee's job the models can do. GPT-4o, whose training data end before the 2024 conference season, referees the papers presented at the 2024 AFA and NBER finance meetings, and we compare its verdicts with publication in the top-three finance journals over the next two years. Papers the model scores one standard deviation higher are 44\% more likely to be published, net of author reputation. The result is not driven by look-ahead bias, as the model does not recall the outcomes. The information comes from its judgements of correctness and exposition. Its judgements of originality and significance carry none, and a referee guide that stresses importance does not help. The split between correctness and contribution holds for accounting papers and for a newer model, GPT-5. LLMs can check whether research is right, but not whether it matters. The technical check can go to the model, while the judgement of contribution stays with people.
